Accumulated knowledge from decompilation attempts. Each insight should help
future attempts match MWCC output more reliably. Query without reading the
whole file: `patterns.py query --grep <word>`.

## Compiler: MWCC 2.0/sp2p2

### Target and flags  <!-- id: mwcc-flags -->

- Target: ARM946E-S (ARMv5TE), primarily Thumb mode
- Flags: `-O4,p -enum int -lang c99 -char signed -inline on,noauto -interworking`
- `-O4,p` means level 4 optimization with peephole; this aggressively reorders code
- `-inline on,noauto` means inlining is allowed but only when explicitly requested (via `inline` keyword or `__attribute__((always_inline))`)

### MWCC errors on int->enum implicit conversion (use named enum constants)  <!-- id: int-to-enum-strict -->

MWCC -W error treats passing an int literal to an enum-typed parameter as an illegal implicit conversion (e.g. Heap_Create(3, 0x30, ...) where params are enum HeapID -> illegal implicit conversion from int to HeapID). Fix: use the named enum constant (HEAP_ID_3, HEAP_ID_48) or an explicit (enum X) cast. Codegen is identical (mov #imm), so this is purely about getting it to compile. The enum HEAP_ID_<N> names are sequential = value N.

### x >> n on a u8/u16 emits asr (signed); retail lsr means the operand is u32/unsigned  <!-- id: u8-u16-rshift-promotes-signed-asr -->

A right shift `x >> n` where x is u8 or u16 promotes x to signed int per C integer promotion, so MWCC emits an arithmetic shift (asr). If the asm shows a logical/unsigned shift (lsr) at that spot, the original operand was an unsigned type that does NOT promote to signed — i.e. u32 (or unsigned int). Fix: declare/cast the operand as u32 (e.g. change a derived param type from u8 to u32, or write ((u32)x >> n)). Left shifts (<<) are unaffected (lsl either way). Seen in unk_0205BFF0.c sub_0205C0A0: `b >> 1` with b as u8 emitted `asr r0,r1,#1` (0x1048); retail had `lsr r0,r1,#1` (0x0848); changing b to u32 fixed it. Note u16 also promotes to signed int, so u16 does NOT give lsr — only u32/unsigned does.

## General Codegen

### Register allocation follows declaration order  <!-- id: regalloc-order -->

- MWCC allocates registers in order: r0-r3 for arguments, r4-r7 for locals (Thumb), r4-r11 for locals (ARM); arguments beyond 4 on the stack; return values in r0 (r0-r1 for 64-bit).
- MWCC assigns callee-saved registers based on variable declaration order in the function. Reordering declarations can swap registers and break matching.
- When the asm uses r6 for variable A and r7 for variable B, try declaring B before A (MWCC sometimes allocates in reverse declaration order).
- Moving a declaration from block scope to function scope changes register lifetime and can affect allocation — match the original variable scoping as closely as C89 allows.
- Functions with many locals: register pressure causes spills to stack in specific order; declaration order is load-bearing.

### Stack frame shape  <!-- id: stack-frame -->

- `push {r4-r7, lr}` / `pop {r4-r7, pc}` is typical Thumb prologue/epilogue.
- `sub sp, #N` for local variables; `add sp, #N` before return; stack variables accessed via `sp + offset`.

### Control flow lowering  <!-- id: control-flow -->

- `if/else` compiles to `cmp + bCC`; `switch` compiles to branch table or cascading compares depending on density.
- Loops compile test-at-top or test-at-bottom; MWCC often hoists loop-invariant loads outside the loop body.
- MWCC sometimes emits `bx` to switch between ARM/Thumb for interworking.

### Data access shapes  <!-- id: data-access -->

- Global data accessed via `ldr rN, =address` (literal pool).
- Struct member access: `ldr rN, [rBase, #offset]`; array access: index * element_size + base.
- Load width reveals the type: `ldrb`=u8, `ldrh`=u16, `ldrsh`=s16, `ldrsb`=s8, `ldr`=u32/pointer.

### Common MWCC idioms  <!-- id: mwcc-idioms -->

- `mov r0, #0` / `mov r0, #1` for FALSE/TRUE returns.
- `add rN, rM, #0` is `mov rN, rM` in Thumb; `lsl r0, r0, #0` is a NOP MWCC sometimes emits.

### Cast a signed param to unsigned to force bhs/blo branches  <!-- id: cast-unsigned-for-branch -->

When a function param is declared signed (e.g. int) per its fixed header, but the asm compares it with an UNSIGNED branch (bhs/blo/bhi/bls) against a u16 table value, force the comparison unsigned by casting at the comparison site: if ((u32)mapsec < p[1]). The cast is free (no instruction) and flips bge/blt -> bhs/blo. A signed int vs u16 promotes both to int and yields signed branches, so the cast is required. Distinguish per-comparison: the loop counter (int i) can stay signed (blt) in the same function while the value comparison is unsigned.

### Raw pointer casts to magic hardware addresses match byte-for-byte  <!-- id: raw-addr-cast-match -->

For files touching fixed DS addresses (0x027FFxxx ROM-header/system-work region), *(u32 *)0xADDR (direct) gives ldr =0xADDR; ldr [r0]; *(u32 *)((u8 *)BASE + off) gives ldr =BASE (loaded once, reused); ldr [rN,#off]. The SAME address can appear both ways in one function (flag check *(u32*)0x027FF00C and header->gamecode at base 0x027FF000 +0xC) -> use both forms. Named HW_ consts (HW_ROM_HEADER_BUF, HW_CARD_ROM_HEADER, HW_CARD_ROM_HEADER_SIZE) match identically to raw literals. A stack struct of size 0xN (FSFile=0x48) gives sub sp,#0xN; read field via *(u32*)((u8*)&s+off).

### Declaration order controls r2/r3 allocation for same-lifetime locals  <!-- id: decl-order-regalloc -->

When two locals share a live range and compete for low Thumb registers (r2/r3), MWCC -O4,p assigns the FIRST-DECLARED variable to the LOWER register. If objdiff shows two functions identical except a consistent r2<->r3 (or rN<->rM) swap, reorder the local declarations to flip the allocation. Example: unk_02017FAC sub_02017FAC needed int i=0 declared before const u16 *p=table so i->r2 (counter/return reg) and p->r3 (walked pointer), matching asm.

### A u16 value loaded via ldrh compares unsigned (bcc/blo) against a constant without a cast  <!-- id: u16-from-ldrh-unsigned-branch -->

When a function param/value is u16 and is read via ldrh (zero-extended), a bounds check like GF_ASSERT(index < 4) compiles to cmp + bcc (unsigned blo) WITHOUT needing an explicit (u32) cast — MWCC knows the ldrh-zero-extended value is non-negative and emits the unsigned branch. This is distinct from the signed-int-vs-u16 case (cast-unsigned-for-branch) where a value already widened to int needs an explicit (u32) cast to flip bge/blt to bhs/blo. Rule of thumb: keep the param u16 (matches the ldrh) and write the plain comparison; only add the (u32) cast when the value is int-typed. Example: overlay_80_02239AF8 ov80_02239AF8 (u16 index).

### Shared store + return as the function fall-off block: hoist value to a temp and store AFTER the switch  <!-- id: shared-store-return-as-fall-off-block -->

When several switch cases each compute a new value, store it to a struct field, and return the same code, MWCC in the retail build often emits ONE shared store+return block as the function LAST/fall-off block (both if/else arms `b` to it), with the cold `default: return 1;` laid out immediately BEFORE it. Three wrong C shapes: (1) store+return inside each case duplicates the store; (2) `break` with the store still in the case body splits the store into its own block plus an extra `b`; (3) `return 0` inside the last case makes MWCC place the cold default block AFTER the return-0 block (wrong order). RIGHT shape: hoist the value to a function-scope temp (`int newState;`), assign it in each arm, then `break`; do the shared store (`st->field = newState;`) and `return 0;` AFTER the switch as the trailing statements. MWCC then merges them into a single fall-off block (`strb; movs r0,#0; add sp; pop`) reached by branches, and places the cold `default: return 1` just before it. Note: `add sp,#N` lands at the END of the last/fall-off block but at the START of a non-last branched return block. Seen in overlay_80_02239BF0.c (ov80_02239C80 state-machine tail). Diagnose: function body matches byte-for-byte except the last ~14 bytes; objdiff shows a SIZE mismatch (inline-jumptable miscount masks it) — disassemble both .o with arm-none-eabi-objdump and compare the tail block order + add-sp placement.

### A flags/bitmask param compared by magnitude with signed blt/bge is int, not u32  <!-- id: flags-param-signed-when-magnitude-compared-blt -->

A parameter you'd instinctively type `u32` because it is used as a bitmask (`flags & (1<<n)`, `tst`) may actually be a signed `int` if the asm ALSO does a magnitude comparison on it with a SIGNED branch. Symptom: `if (flags >= (1<<N))` emitted as `cmp rX, #imm; blo/bcc` (unsigned) in your C, but the target asm uses `cmp rX, #imm; blt` (signed) at that gate. The bitwise tests (`tst`) are sign-agnostic, so they give no clue — only the magnitude compare reveals the signedness. Fix: declare the param `int` (or s32). The `&`/`tst` codegen is unchanged; only the `>=`/`<` flips from unsigned `blo/bhs` to signed `blt/bge`. This is the INVERSE of [[cast-unsigned-for-branch]] (which adds a (u32) cast to a signed param to FORCE unsigned branches) and [[u16-from-ldrh-unsigned-branch]]. Seen in overlay_01_021EA8E0.c ov01_021EA910 (the `flags >= 0x1000` gate before NNS_G3dGlbPolygonAttr): u32 flags emitted bcc, int flags emitted the matching blt.

### A down-counting loop with subs;bne needs an UNSIGNED counter (signed int -> hoisted decrement + cmp;bgt)  <!-- id: downcount-copy-loop-needs-unsigned-counter-for-subs-bne -->

A fixed-count copy/fill loop whose asm is `movs rN,#K; .L: <body>; subs rN,#1; bne .L` (decrement LAST, branch-if-nonzero) must use an UNSIGNED counter in C. Writing `int i = K; do { body } while (--i);` does NOT match: MWCC -O4,p proves a signed `i` stays >= 0 (range analysis), converts the `!=0` test to a signed `> 0`, and HOISTS the `subs` up into the body — which then forces a separate `cmp rN,#0; bgt` at the bottom (the intervening pointer `adds` clobber the Z flag). Result: function is 2 bytes too big (objdiff SIZE +2). FIX: make the counter `u32` (or any unsigned): `u32 i = K; do { body } while (--i);`. Unsigned forbids the signed `bgt` form, so MWCC keeps the decrement at the bottom and emits `subs;bne` reusing the Z flag. Also: declare the source/walker pointers in the SAME order the asm sets them up (e.g. `p=src` before `dst=base+off` if asm does `adds rSrc` then `adds rDst`) — decl order drives the two setup `adds` order. Seen in frontier_system.c ov80_0222AAD8/AAF8 (8x u16 copy of FrontierSystemWork+0x24).

### MI_CpuFill32/inline wrappers that REORDER args can cache a simple-load arg across a call arg — extract the call to a temp  <!-- id: inline-fn-swapped-arg-caches-across-call -->

MI_CpuFill32(dest, data, size) is a static inline that forwards to MIi_CpuClear32(data, dest, size) — it SWAPS the first two args so `data` becomes arg0. When you call MI_CpuFill32(callResult(...), self->field, N) with dest being a CALL and data a simple field load, MWCC evaluates arg0 (=data, the field) FIRST and must keep it live across the dest call → it lands in a callee-saved reg, widening push {..} and adding instructions (objdiff: function a few bytes too big, extra pushed reg). The asm computed the call first, then loaded the fill value after. Fix: hoist the call into its own statement so it is sequenced before the field load: `void *p = callResult(...); MI_CpuFill32(p, self->field, N);`. Now neither survives a call → both caller-saved, push narrows to match. Note: plain memset(callResult, val, N) does NOT hit this (memset is a real extern, args eval left-to-right so the call/dest is arg0 and evaluated first). Only inline wrappers that permute arg order trigger it. Seen in unk_02014A08 sub_02014C08 (MI_CpuFill32 of sub_02014A4C result). Related: [[no-cache-reloaded-pointer-across-calls]], [[hoist-size-local-callee-saved]].

### A u8/u16 loop counter narrows on ++ and may force an unsigned branch; use int when the asm increments full-width with a signed/range compare  <!-- id: narrowing-loop-counter-int-for-fullwidth-incr-and-compare -->

A loop counter typed u8 or u16 makes MWCC (1) NARROW it on each increment (`adds rN,#1; lsls#24/#16; lsrs#24/#16` for u8/u16 — 2 extra bytes per loop), and (2) pick an UNSIGNED branch for its bound test. If the target asm increments the counter full-width (`adds rN,rN,#1` with no narrowing) AND/OR compares it with a SIGNED branch (cmp; bgt/ble), the counter was `int` (or s32). Switching the counter to `int` drops the narrowing and makes `counter <= someU8Field` a signed compare (the u8 field promotes to int; the int counter keeps it signed). Conversely, if the asm shows an UNSIGNED bound branch (bcc/bls) with NO narrowing on the counter, use `u32` (a u16 field on the other side promotes to u32, unsigned compare, and u32++ does not narrow). Seen in unk_02014A08: sub_02014C60 loop index needed u32 (unsigned bcc bound, no narrow); sub_02014CBC scanline counter needed int (signed bgt/ble vs u8 start/end fields, full-width ++). Diagnose: objdiff SIZE +2 per loop from the lsls/lsrs narrow, plus a blt<->bcc or bgt<->bhi opcode swap. Related: [[downcount-copy-loop-needs-unsigned-counter-for-subs-bne]], [[param-narrowing]].

### Bitfield extract for a switch/index: (v & (k<<n)) >> n emits mask-first (mov;lsl;and;lsr); (v >> n) & k emits shift-first — match the asm form  <!-- id: bitfield-extract-mask-first-vs-shift-first -->

Extracting a sub-field `(v >> n) & mask` has two equivalent codegen shapes MWCC picks based on source SYNTAX, not value: (1) `(v >> n) & k` -> shift-first: `lsrs rA, v, #n; movs rB, #k; ands rA, rB` (3 insns). (2) `(v & (k << n)) >> n` -> mask-first: `movs rB, #k; lsls rB, #n; ands rB, v; lsrs rB, #n` (4 insns; builds the shifted mask via mov+lsl rather than a literal-pool load when k<<n is a shifted small constant). If the asm shows the 4-insn mask-first form (common for a switch discriminant or a packed-field read), write the masked form `(v & 0xMASK) >> n` with the literal mask spelled out (e.g. `(v & 0x1C000000) >> 26` for bits 26-28). Writing `(v >> 26) & 7` gives the shorter shift-first form and a byte mismatch. MWCC builds the mask 0x1C000000 = 7<<26 as `movs #7; lsls #26` (no pool word). Seen in unk_0202068C sub_0202094C (texture-format switch on bits 26-28). The width/height field reads in the same function used the SAME masked form `(v & 0x700000) >> 20`. Related: [[bitfield-lsls-lsrs]], [[packed-lookup-table-is-bitfield-struct]].

### An init loop that fills count items should bound on the STORED field (obj->count), not the param — the field reloads each iter and frees the param register  <!-- id: manager-count-reload-vs-param-in-init-loop -->

A constructor that stores a count then loops to init each slot — `obj->count = count; for (i = 0; i < ???; i++) init(&obj->items[i]);` — must use `obj->count` (the stored field) as the loop bound, NOT the `count` parameter. The asm reloads `obj->count` from memory every iteration (because the init() call may invalidate it) and REUSES the count parameter register for the walking byte-offset, so only 3 callee-saved regs are needed (push {r4,r5,r6,lr}). Writing `i < count` (the param) keeps the param live in a callee-saved register across the whole loop, needing a 4th callee-saved reg -> wider push (push {r3,r4,r5,r6,r7,lr}) and a 2-byte size delta. Fix: bound on `obj->count`. Diagnose: objdiff SIZE -2 with a wider push and an extra adds r5,r6,#0-style reg copy. Seen in unk_0202068C sub_0202068C (vs its sibling sub_02020740 which already looped on manager->count and matched). Related: [[no-cache-reloaded-pointer-across-calls]].

### A by-value small-struct param whose address is taken forces `push {r0-r3}` arg-homing; pass the fields as scalars + a coalesced local struct to avoid it  <!-- id: byval-small-struct-param-addressed-homes-args -->

When a function takes a small (<=16-byte) struct BY VALUE in arg registers and then takes its ADDRESS (e.g. passes &param to a helper), MWCC homes ALL incoming arg registers with a leading `push {r0,r1,r2,r3}` plus a matching heavy epilogue at every return (`pop {r4,r5,r6,r7}; pop {r3}; add sp,#16; bx r3`), inflating the function by 16+ bytes and shifting every stack offset. The retail build avoids this: it passes the struct's COMPONENTS as separate scalar params and declares a LOCAL struct that MWCC COALESCES onto the scalar params' spill slots (so the only stores are the normal arg spills, e.g. `str r2,[sp,#0x30]; str r3,[sp,#0x34]`), then takes the address of that local. No push {r0-r3} appears because the addressed object is a genuine local, not a register param. Fix: change `f(.., MeshPoint query, ..)` to `f(.., fx32 x, fx32 z, ..)` + `MeshPoint query; query.x = x; query.y = z;` and pass `&query`; use `query.x`/`query.y` (not x/z) at later use sites so they reload from the coalesced slot across calls. Diagnose via objdiff: prologue `push {r0,r1,r2,r3}` + sub sp smaller by 0x10, and the multi-instruction `pop;pop;add sp;bx r3` epilogue at each return. Seen in overlay_01_021FAD1C ov01_021FAE50 (the (x,z) query point). Related: [[stack-slot-reverse-decl-order]].

### For small (u8) array loops, use the real struct-array field / a typed pointer so MWCC keeps [base, index] addressing; a raw ((u8*)p)[i] cast plus a separate loaded temp can trigger pointer strength-reduction  <!-- id: u8-array-loop-indexed-vs-walking -->

In a `for (i=0;i<N;i++)` loop over u8 arrays where element size is 1, indexed addressing `ldrb rD,[base,i]` is already optimal (no scaling), so the matching codegen keeps the base pointers loop-invariant and reuses the counter `i` as the index. Writing the body as `((u8*)a2)[i]` together with a separate `u8 v = ((u8*)a2)[i];` temp pushed MWCC sp2p2 onto its induction-variable / strength-reduction path: it introduced two extra `adds rBase,#1` per iteration (walking pointers) AND flipped the `cmp` operand order — +4 bytes, no match. Fix: access through the actual struct array field (`ribbons->ribbons[i]`) and a typed local pointer (`u8 *src = a2;`), and compare directly (`ribbons->ribbons[i] != src[i]`) with no intermediate temp. That restored `ldrb r1,[r5,r2]` / `ldrb r0,[r4,r2]` / `cmp r0,r1` / `strb r1,[r4,r2]`. Lesson: prefer genuine array-subscript expressions over raw-cast subscripts + hoisted temps when you need indexed addressing to survive. (unk_0208F658.s sub_0208F74C)

### When two calls use the same logical value via different access paths, match the exact source expression: `obj->ptr->field` reloads from memory; a local `T *p=...; p->field` uses the cached register  <!-- id: struct-member-reload-vs-local-var -->

In sub_020961D8, EasyChat_CreateArgs(...) takes saveData as `work->fieldSystem->saveData` -> MWCC emits `ldr r2,[r4](=work->fieldSystem); ldr r2,[r2,#0xc]` (reload the pointer from the struct), while the very next Save_Misc_Get(...) takes `fieldSystem->saveData` -> `ldr r0,[r5,#0xc]` (uses the local FieldSystem* kept in r5). Both are the same pointer value, but the source expression differs and so does the codegen (extra reload vs cached reg). If a call site is 4 bytes short and the asm has an extra `ldr rN,[base]` before the field load, the source went through the struct member (obj->ptr->field), not the local variable. Pick per-call to match.

### Match the asm return-block placement: `if(x==NULL) return A; body; return B;` emits the A-return INLINE; the asm form with the early-return at the END (beq-to-end) comes from `if(x!=NULL){ body; return B; } return A;`  <!-- id: early-return-block-placement -->

For a guard like null-check, MWCC lays out the return blocks by source structure. `if(p==NULL){return 0;} body; return 1;` -> `cmp;bne body; movs r0,#0; pop; body...; return1` (the return-0 is inline right after the branch). The asm often instead has `cmp; beq END; body; return1; END: return0` (the failure return is a block at the very end, reached by branch). To reproduce that, invert: `if(p!=NULL){ body; return 1; } return 0;`. Same logic, but the body is the fall-through and the failure-return is last. Seen in unk_020379A0.s sub_02037C0C (u32, return 1/0) and sub_02037C44 (ptr, return entry/NULL).

### For a 2-byte-stride pair store, use u8 arr[N][2] + arr[i][0/1] so the +1 folds into the str immediate ((base+i*2)+#1); a flat u8 arr[2N] + arr[i*2+1] can instead emit base+(i*2+1) via a register index  <!-- id: pair-array-2d-vs-flat-imm-offset -->

unk_020379A0.s unk00 is 8 two-byte slots. Flat `u8 unk00[0x10]` with `unk00[a0*2+1]=v` produced `adds rIdx,rRow,#1; strb [base,rIdx]` (the +1 went into the index) in sub_02037B6C, mismatching the asm `adds r0,base,rRow; strb [r0,#1]` (+1 in the store immediate). Switching to `u8 unk00[8][2]` and `unk00[a0][1]=v` makes MWCC compute the row base (base+a0*2) then use immediate #1 -> match. Subtlety: the READ in sub_02037BA0 matched with BOTH forms (same bytes), but the WRITE-with-reload context in sub_02037B6C only matched with the 2D array. When a pair/tuple store is off by the +1 placement, model the data as [N][k] not [N*k].

### For a branchy float->fx32 conversion ((cond)?(x+0.5f):(x-0.5f) then cast), compute a `f32 tmp` in the if/else and apply ONE (fx32)tmp after the merge so _ffix is shared, not duplicated per branch  <!-- id: float-to-fx32-shared-ffix -->

sub_0205BED8 converts u16 args to fx32 with rounding: `(fx32)((a!=0) ? 0.5f+(f32)(a<<12) : (f32)(a<<12)-0.5f)`. Writing the (fx32) cast inside each branch (`env->x = (fx32)(...)` in both arms) duplicates the _ffix call (and the store) -> +8 bytes. The asm instead does `_fflt`/`_fadd` or `_fsub` per branch, then a SINGLE `_ffix` at the merge, then one store. Reproduce with a float temp: `f32 t; if(a){t=0.5f+(f32)(a<<12);}else{t=(f32)(a<<12)-0.5f;} env->x=(fx32)t;`. The (f32)(a<<12) IS duplicated per branch (matches asm) — only the trailing cast/store is shared. MWCC soft-float intrinsics: (f32)int=_fflt, +/-= _fadd/_fsub, (s32)f32=_ffix, f32*f32=_fmul; FX_Mul = FX_MulInline = ((s64)v1*v2+0x800)>>12 (= _ll_mul + shift).

### When a count/index loop is off only by which callee-saved register holds the counter vs the bound, swap the local DECLARATION order (declare the loop index before the count)  <!-- id: loop-index-decl-order-regalloc -->

Save_GetPartyLead mismatched by 7 bytes that were purely register fields: asm had count=r5,i=r4 but `u16 count=..; u16 i;` gave count=r4,i=r5. Declaring the index first (`u16 i; u16 count=Party_GetCount(..);`) flipped MWCC register assignment to match. (The near-identical Save_GetPartyLeadAlive matched as-is because its extra `mon` local shifted the allocation.) General lever: when two same-lifetime locals land in swapped registers, reorder their declarations; the names are irrelevant, the order drives MWCC callee-saved assignment.

### A function that InitBgFromTemplate()s N backgrounds from N different static const BgTemplates uses N SEPARATE stack BgTemplate locals (struct-copy each), not one reused local  <!-- id: bg-init-separate-template-locals -->

ov33_0225D720 copies sBgTemplate_4/5/6 (each via ldmia/stmia) into THREE distinct stack slots (sp+0x38, +0x1c, +0) and passes &each to InitBgFromTemplate — stack frame 0x54 (3*0x1c), not 0x1c. Reusing a single `BgTemplate template; template=sBgTemplate_4; Init(..&template); template=sBgTemplate_5; ...` collapses to one slot (frame 0x1c) and mismatches. Declare `BgTemplate template1, template2, template3;` (first-declared -> highest offset sp+0x38). Related landed fixes for touchscreen-menu overlays: GX_SetBankForSubBG uses GX_VRAM_SUB_BG_32_H (0x80=GX_VRAM_H) / GX_VRAM_SUB_OBJ_16_I (0x100=GX_VRAM_I) — the H/I banks, NOT 128_C/128_D (C/D=0x80? no: C=4,D=8); count-bounded window loops use `u32 i` (unmasked, bcc) when the body strength-reduces &windows[i] to a walking pointer; a u8 struct field passed straight to a u8 fn param should be declared u8 (not int) to avoid a (u8) truncation.

### When a precondition assert path RETURNS (does not fall through to the function body), use explicit `if (assertFails) { GF_AssertFail(); return; }` — NOT GF_ASSERT(cond)  <!-- id: assert-return-not-gf-assert -->

GF_ASSERT(expr) = ((expr) ? (void)0 : GF_AssertFail()) and GF_AssertFail is `void GF_AssertFail(void)` (NOT noreturn). So `GF_ASSERT(cond); body;` compiles to `cmp;bne L; bl GF_AssertFail; L: body` — the assert-fail path FALLS THROUGH to body. If the asm instead shows `cmp; b<skip> body; bl GF_AssertFail; pop(return); body:` (the assert path returns and body is a separate block reached only when the assert passes), the source was an explicit `if (cond==0){ GF_AssertFail(); return; } body;` (or `if(cond!=0){...}` for an inverted assert). unk_02055244.s: CallTask_LeaveOverworld/PaletteFadeUntilFinished/FadeFromBlack assert sub_0203DF7C(fs)!=0 (if(==0){fail;return;}); CallTask_RestoreOverworld asserts it ==0 (if(!=0){fail;return;}). All 11 fns matched first build with this form. (If GF_AssertFail WERE noreturn, GF_ASSERT would be correct — check the prototype.)

### && (all-pass->return 1) vs || (any-fail->return 0) controls return-block placement  <!-- id: bounds-check-and-vs-or-return-layout -->

A multi-term bounds/validity check compiled by MWCC places the two return epilogues in an order that depends on how you write it. `if (A||B||...||H) return 0; return 1;` puts the shared `return 0` block inline right after the checks and forces the LAST term to be inverted (ble vs bgt) to branch over it to `return 1` at the end. The asm form that keeps `return 1` as the inline fall-through with a single shared `return 0` block at the very end (all N checks forward-branch blt/bgt to it) is produced by the && form: `if (A2 && B2 && ... && H2) return 1; return 0;` where each term is the negation (maxX>=out->x, minX<=out->x, ...). Match the source to whichever return is the fall-through in the asm. Saw this in sub_02020F4C (8-term AABB check).

### MWCC assigns local stack slots in declaration order, first-declared at highest address  <!-- id: local-stack-slot-order-equals-decl-order -->

When a function is byte-identical to the asm EXCEPT the sp+N offsets in every load/store (and the VEC_* out-pointer args), the cause is local declaration ORDER. MWCC lays out stack-homed locals so the first-declared gets the highest sp offset, each subsequent one lower. To match, reorder the C declarations so (high->low) = asm's (highest-offset-local ... lowest). Example: GetDistanceFromPointToLine matched once declarations were reordered to lineDir, toPoint, diff, proj, zero (asm slots 68,56,44,32,20). Corollary: two FX_Modf integer-part outputs need two distinct named locals (intPartX, intPartY) to get two stack slots rather than one reused slot (sub_02020F4C).

### Unsigned countdown loop counter -> subs/bne; signed int -> cmp/bgt  <!-- id: countdown-loop-counter-signedness -->

For a `do { ... } while (--i)` countdown loop, the counter's signedness changes the loop epilogue. A SIGNED `int i` lets MWCC use the i>0 shortcut and emits `subs i,#1; <other body op>; cmp i,#0; bgt` — the decrement floats away from the branch and needs a separate cmp (extra 2 bytes + possible nop). An UNSIGNED `u32 i` forces a plain nonzero test, emitting `<body op>; subs i,#1; bne` with the decrement adjacent to the branch (no cmp). If a countdown loop is ~4 bytes too big with a cmp+bgt where the asm has bne, switch the counter to u32. Saw in ov01_021FD3F8 (overlay_01_021FD1B8.s). Pair with caching loop-invariant struct fields (e.g. mgr->count) in locals so they survive calls in callee regs instead of being reloaded each iteration.

### Split a nested call into a local to force a struct-field reload across the call  <!-- id: split-call-to-force-struct-field-reload -->

When code is f(g(s->ptr->a), s->ptr->b, ...), MWCC may evaluate the non-call argument s->ptr->b BEFORE the call g(), caching s->ptr in a callee register so it survives g - using an extra callee reg and shifting the whole function register allocation. The asm instead RELOADS s->ptr after g() returns. To match, hoist the call into its own statement: T x = g(s->ptr->a); f(x, s->ptr->b, ...). Now s->ptr->b is evaluated after g() returns so MWCC reloads s->ptr (cannot prove g did not modify it) - no extra callee reg, allocation matches. Saw in unk_020192D0.c case 4.

### Compute `range = hi - lo` INSIDE each if/else branch (not after the merge) to get the subtract before a following call  <!-- id: compute-range-inside-each-branch-for-eager-subtract -->

For `return lo + LCRandom() % (hi - lo)` where lo/hi are assigned in an if/else, MWCC evaluates the modulus operands left-to-right: it calls LCRandom() FIRST, then computes `(hi-lo)` AFTER the call (keeps both hi and lo live across the call, subtracts after -> `bl; subs r1,r5,r4`). If the target asm computes the range BEFORE the call (`subs r5,r0,r4; bl LCRandom; ...`), it kept only {lo, range} live across the call. To match, compute the range inside EACH branch using the just-loaded values: `if (cond) { lo = t[i].c; range = t[i].d - lo; } else { lo = t[i].a; range = t[i].b - lo; } return lo + LCRandom() % range;`. The subtraction then sits in each branch (before the merge/call), exactly like the asm, and only lo+range survive the call. A single post-merge `range = hi - lo;` statement does NOT force this — MWCC still sinks the subtract past the call. Verified in overlay_80_02238034 ov80_02238034 (random level in [lo,hi)).

### Parenthesize `(a2+1) + 7*a1` to control which addend is the final-add's first operand (MWCC preloads the mul constant)  <!-- id: addend-grouping-controls-mul-add-schedule -->

MWCC evaluates `(a2 + 1) + 7 * a1` as: `mov r0,#7` (preload mul constant early), `adds r3,r2,#1` (the (a2+1) addend), `muls r0,r1` (7*a1), `adds r0,r3,r0` (range r3 first). Writing `7 * a1 + a2 + 1` instead parses as `((7*a1)+a2)+1` -> `muls; adds r0,r2,r0; adds r0,r0,#1` (different schedule, +1 is a separate trailing add). The grouping of the constant-fold determines the final `add` operand order (`add r0,r3,r0` vs `add r0,r0,#1`). Match by grouping the source exactly as the value is built in asm. Verified in overlay_80_02238034 ov80_02238034. Combine with making the multiplied index `u32` so `if (a1 >= 8)` and the array index use unsigned `blo` not signed `blt` (see [[cast-unsigned-for-branch]]).

### Assign a u32 function return to an int local before signed arithmetic, or `(a - b)/2` becomes an unsigned shift (lsr)  <!-- id: u32-call-return-makes-divide-an-unsigned-shift -->

`(width<<3) - FontID_String_GetWidth(...)` then `/2`: FontID_String_GetWidth returns u32, so the subtraction promotes to unsigned and `/2` compiles to a single `lsrs #1` (logical). If the target asm does SIGNED division (`subs; lsrs rX,#31; adds; asrs rY,#1` — the sign-bit round-toward-zero idiom), the original kept the value SIGNED: store the u32 return into an `int` local first (`int width = FontID_String_GetWidth(...); x = ((win->width<<3) - width)/2;`). `int - int` is signed, so `/2` emits the signed-div idiom and matches. A plain subtract (no division) is unaffected (same bytes signed/unsigned), so this only bites on `/`, `%`, `>>` of the difference. Also for the align dispatch in the same function (ov01_021F4234): a `switch (align) { case 1:..; case 2:..; }` emits the asm's `cmp #1;beq;cmp #2;beq;b` jump-to-body dispatch, whereas `if/else if` emits interleaved `cmp;bne` skips. Seen in overlay_01_021F3F50 ov01_021F4234. Related: [[switch-form-avoids-equality-or-range-opt]].

### Zero a small stack struct with an aggregate initializer `{0,0,0}`, not field-by-field, to get base-pointer stores  <!-- id: aggregate-init-zeroes-vec-via-base-pointer -->

`VecFx32 v; v.x=0; v.y=0; v.z=0;` makes MWCC emit sp-DIRECT stores (`movs rZ,#0; str rZ,[sp,#off]; str rZ,[sp,#off+4]; str rZ,[sp,#off+8]`). The retail code for the same zero-init uses a BASE POINTER (`add rP,sp,#off; movs rZ,#0; str rZ,[rP]; str rZ,[rP,#4]; str rZ,[rP,#8]`) — produced by an AGGREGATE INITIALIZER: `VecFx32 v = {0,0,0};`. Switching field-assignments to the initializer flipped overlay_01_021FE780 ov01_021FE7DC from 38 diffs to 7 and ov01_021FE8B0 from 6 to ~2 (the rest fixed by also loading the first call arg into a local before the init so &v lands directly in the arg register r1). Use the initializer whenever the asm zeroes a VecFx32/MtxFx/struct local through a held base pointer. Combine with [[decl-order-regalloc]] for which stack slot the struct gets.

### Hoist a function-call argument that must occupy r0 ABOVE a sibling computation, via a temp, to match the asm's register choice  <!-- id: evaluate-call-arg-before-sibling-computation-for-arg-reg -->

`sub_0206121C(MapObject_GetFieldSystem(obj), &pos)` preceded by `pos.x = (a<<16)+k; pos.z=(b<<16)+k;` — MWCC evaluates the position stores FIRST (using r0/r1), then calls MapObject_GetFieldSystem as the 1st arg. If the target asm calls MapObject_GetFieldSystem FIRST (r0=fieldSystem, held across the position math, so the math uses r1/r2), hoist it into a temp BEFORE the computation: `FieldSystem *fs = MapObject_GetFieldSystem(obj); pos.x=...; pos.z=...; sub_0206121C(fs, &pos);`. The temp keeps fieldSystem in r0 across the position math, shifting the math up one register (r0/r1 -> r1/r2) to match. Diagnose: same instructions, every register shifted by one. Seen in overlay_01_021FE780 ov01_021FE7DC (fixed the last 7 diffs).

### `&work->member->field` after `work->member = src` reuses the stored value; avoids re-reading src (but read ORDER may still differ)  <!-- id: reuse-just-stored-member-avoids-source-reread -->

In a callback that does `work->unk7c = data->manager; ...(&data->manager->unk4)...`, MWCC RE-READS data->manager for the second access (+2 bytes, aliasing-conservative after the store). Writing `&work->unk7c->unk4` instead (the member just stored) makes MWCC reuse the stored register value -> no re-read, size-correct. CAVEAT: this can leave a read-ORDER difference -- the retail code reads BOTH data fields (manager@4, fieldSystem@0) into regs FIRST, then does all the stores; the natural C `work->unk78=data->fieldSystem; work->unk7c=data->manager;` reads offset 0 first. Neither caching `manager` in a local (reorders fieldSystem to r0 + materializes work early) nor swapping the assignment order (breaks the store order / reloads work->unk7c) reproduces the batched read-then-store schedule. Seen identically in overlay_01_021FED9C ov01_021FEE64 and overlay_01_021FEC38 ov01_021FED14 (8/9 each) -- the camera/3D-effect family's data-copy cb1.

### Stack-passed u16 params stored to wide fields: declare them int/u32, not u16 (Thumb ldrh can't use sp, forcing an extra base-pointer add)  <!-- id: u16-stack-param-as-int-avoids-ldrh-basepointer -->

A function whose 5th/6th args are passed on the stack and just copied into u32 struct fields: if you declare those params `u16`, MWCC reads them with `ldrh`, and because Thumb `ldrh Rd,[Rn,#imm]` requires a LOW base register (sp/r13 is illegal), it must first emit `add rN,sp,#k` then `ldrh [rN,#off]` -- an extra instruction and a wrong register schedule. The retail asm reads them with `ldr rN,[sp,#off]` (sp-direct word load), i.e. the params are int/u32-width. Declare the stack params `u32` (or int) so MWCC emits the sp-direct `ldr`. When the public header (used by the CALLER) declares them `u16`, keep that header frozen and use a LOCAL prototype with the int/u32 types in the defining .c (split-header / IPA discipline). Verified on unk_020979A8 (sub_020979A8 constructor: a4/a5 sp[24]/sp[28]). See [[ipa-split-header]].

### A u16->u32 widening store of a register param inserts a cast node that changes the MWCC list-scheduler tie-break; declare the param u32 to match  <!-- id: widening-cast-of-param-perturbs-scheduler -->

Even a REGISTER-passed param (not just stack) can break matching purely by type width. unk_020979A8's `a3` (u16) stored to a u32 field `work->unk4=a3` compiled with every instruction correct but TWO swapped: the asm hoists the LoadArea-arg base copy `adds r1,r4,#0` and the `a3` reload ahead of the `unk2` store, mine emitted them after. The cause was the u16->u32 widening cast node in the IR perturbing the list scheduler's tie-break between equally-ready instructions. Declaring `a3` as `u32` (no widening cast; the spilled r3 is already a full word) removed the cast and reproduced the asm's exact instruction order -> full match. Rule: when a param is only ever stored to a wider field and the asm shows no zero/sign-extend, declare the param at the field's width. Pairs with [[u16-stack-param-as-int-avoids-ldrh-basepointer]].

### Public headers often over-widen params to int; stack params stored to byte fields are read ldrb/ldrsb (sp-illegal -> negative-base trick). Declare them u8/s8 via split-header.  <!-- id: public-header-overwidens-narrow-stack-params -->

Mirror image of [[u16-stack-param-as-int-avoids-ldrh-basepointer]]. A shared public header (e.g. include/unk_0201956C.h, used by a matched caller) frequently declares params as `int` for convenience, but the FUNCTION reads narrow stack params at byte width. Tells: the asm reads a 5th/6th stack param with `ldrb`/`ldrsb` AND uses the negative-base trick `ldr r3,=0xFFFFFFF8; add r3,sp; ldrb r2,[r3,#0x10]` (because Thumb ldrb/ldrsb/ldrh cannot use sp as base, just like ldrh). If you declare such a param `int`, MWCC emits a plain `ldr [sp,#k]` (word) and the bytes diverge. Fix: declare the defining function's param at the field's width (u8 if stored to a u8 field / read ldrb; s8 if stored to an s8 field / read ldrsb) using a LOCAL prototype, and DON'T include the public header (keep it frozen at int for the caller). On unk_0201956C this fixed sub_020198FC (a4->u8), sub_02019B70 (a4,a5->s8). Related: struct velocity fields read via ldrsb in `x += field` are s8 not u8 (sub_02019978); for-loop counters with `blo` compare and no 16-bit wrap are u32 not u16 (sub_02019934, sub_020195C0).

### Place a VecFx32 zero-init exactly where the asm zeroes it by declaring it mid-block (C99) — aggregate init gives the base-pointer store form, the declaration point gives the position  <!-- id: midblock-aggregate-init-controls-zero-fill-position -->

Two separate facts combine. (1) [[aggregate-init-zeroes-vec-via-base-pointer]]: `VecFx32 v = {0,0,0}` emits `add rN,sp,#k; str r0,[rN]; str r0,[rN,#4]; str r0,[rN,#8]` (base-pointer), whereas field stores `v.x=0;v.y=0;v.z=0` emit sp-direct `str r0,[sp,#k]`. (2) MWCC emits the aggregate initializer AT the declaration point, not hoisted to function entry. So when the retail asm zeroes the vec in the MIDDLE of the function (e.g. between two struct-field stores), declare the vec with a mid-block/nested-scope declaration there: `... data.unk8 = f(); { VecFx32 vec = {0,0,0}; data.mapObject = x; g(&vec,&data); }`. Declaring it at the top with aggregate init gives the right FORM but the wrong POSITION (hoisted up); field assignments in the right position give the right position but wrong form. The nested block gets both. Verified on ov01_02200730 (overlay_01_022006A8). Project builds -lang c99 so mid-block decls are legal.

### Camera/3D-effect family (ov01_021F1348 cluster): a cb1 that BLOCK-copies the data struct (work->sub = *sub_02068D98(p)) matches cleanly, unlike the field-by-field re-read cb1 that is the family holdout  <!-- id: camera-family-blockcopy-cb1-matches -->

The map-object 3D-effect family (constructor via ov01_021F1430, spawn via ov01_021F1620 with a const template {sizeof(work), cb1, cb1, cb2, cb2}, data fetched in cb1 via sub_02068D98) comes in two cb1 shapes. The FIELD-BY-FIELD shape (work->unk78=data->fieldSystem; work->unk7c=data->manager; ...(&data->manager->unk4)) is a persistent MWCC read-order/scheduling holdout (overlay_01_021FEE64/021FED14 etc.). The BLOCK-COPY shape — where cb1 does a whole-struct assignment `work->copiedData = *(MyData*)sub_02068D98(param0)` (4 words -> 2x ldmia/stmia) then reads members out of the copy — matches with zero fuss. overlay_01_022006A8 (9 fns) matched fully this way. When picking the cb1 C shape, prefer the single struct-assignment when the asm shows ldmia/stmia (not N field loads/stores). Define per-file manager/work/data structs and use LOCAL externs for the cluster fns (do NOT include overlay_01_021F1348.h / overlay_01.h — they conflict). [[reuse-just-stored-member-avoids-source-reread]]

### A flags byte written via manual mask at bit0 + bitfields at other bits needs a union {u8 raw; struct bits}  <!-- id: flags-byte-union-manual-mask-bit0 -->

When a byte holds several 1-bit flags set by different functions and the asm shows NO (u8) narrow for the bit-0 flag (just ldrb; bic #1; and #1(val); orr; strb) but DOES narrow for bits 1-4 ((u8)val via lsls#24/lsrs#24 then the <<31>>(31-pos) insert), the bit-0 write is a MANUAL mask `b->raw = (b->raw & ~1) | (val & 1)` while the others are bitfield assignments. A bitfield assignment of an int value ALWAYS narrows to the u8 storage first; at bit position 0 that yields a spurious (u8) the retail build lacks. Model as union { u8 raw; struct { u8 flag0:1; u8 flag1:1; ... } bits; } and use raw for the bit-0 manual mask, .bits.flagN for the rest (those match plain `= val`). Seen in unk_02068FC8: sub_020692A0 a0->bit0 (manual) vs sub_020692C4/308/3AC gender/dexEnabled/a1/sigExists->bits.

### `x &= ~1; x &= 1;` as TWO separate load-modify-stores = a bitfield struct {u32 a:1; u32 b:31}, not a plain u32  <!-- id: two-rmw-clear-is-bitfield-struct -->

An array element zeroed with the asm emitting TWO full RMW (ldr;bic #1;str; ldr;and #1;str) — not one merged ldr;bic;and;str — is a bitfield struct: `struct { u32 bit0:1; u32 rest:31; } arr[N];` written `arr[i].bit0 = 0; arr[i].rest = 0;` (bit0=0 -> bic #1; rest=0 -> and #1 keeping bit0). A plain `u32 arr[N]` with `arr[i] &= ~1; arr[i] &= 1;` makes MWCC merge the two ops AND strength-reduce the index to a walking pointer; the bitfield-array form keeps &arr loop-invariant with [base, i*4] indexing and two distinct stores. Seen in unk_02068FC8 sub_0206940C (rec->unk48[8]).

### An intervening store to a sibling field through the same base pointer invalidates MWCC's cached value -> forces a reload  <!-- id: adjacent-field-store-forces-reload -->

Clamping consecutive fields: the asm RELOADS a field for its check (ldr field; cmp) for some fields but compares the source register directly for others. The reload appears when another store through the same base sits BETWEEN the field's store and its check (MWCC drops the cached value after any same-base store, conservative aliasing). To get the reload form: emit both stores first then both checks (`s->a=x; s->b=y; if(s->a>M)..; if(s->b>M)..;`). To get the no-reload form: keep store and check adjacent with no intervening same-base store (`s->a=x; if(x>M)..;`). Seen in unk_02068FC8 sub_020693AC (unk3c/unk40 reload via the in-between store; unk38/unk44 compare the param).

### A field-by-field cb1 in the ov01_021F1348 camera family DOES match when it copies flat data fields (no nested manager->unk4 reread)  <!-- id: camera-family-fieldbyfield-cb1-can-match-without-nested-aliasing -->

Not every field-by-field cb1 is the holdout from [[camera-family-blockcopy-cb1-matches]]. The holdout reads through a NESTED pointer (work->unk7c=data->manager; ...&data->manager->unk4) which creates an aliasing/read-order schedule MWCC won't reproduce. A cb1 that just copies FLAT fields of the sub_02068D98 data into the work (work->unk18=data->unk8; work->unk14=data->unk4; work->unk10=data->unk0, in descending order) matches first try as plain field assignments. ov01_021FE4FC matched this way (it even keeps a dead `work->unk10 = sub_02068D90(param0)` store that is overwritten by data->unk0 — reproduce it verbatim; MWCC keeps the dead store). Manager-with-arrays files in this family (10x sub-objects + 10x NNSG3dRenderObj) decompile cleanly using src/field/overlay_01_021FE780.c as the template: per-file structs, local externs, NO cluster header. Jump-table address-calculators (ov01_021FE2DC/35C) show spurious objdiff SIZE diffs (data-region mapping-symbol miscount) — confirm with chiri pkg -- compare. The a4-data and VecFx32 position locals in the spawn fn need position declared FIRST (first-declared = highest sp offset).

## Matching Tricks

### Small source changes that move codegen  <!-- id: decl-order-tricks -->

- Variable declaration order affects register allocation.
- `u32` vs `int` can change sign-extension instructions; `size / 2` vs `size >> 1` can differ at -O4 — try both.
- Ternary `a ? b : c` can produce different code than `if/else`.
- Assigning to a temp variable vs direct use changes register lifetimes.
- `NELEMS(array)` (sizeof/sizeof) matches constant folding.
- Casting to `(void)` suppresses warnings without changing codegen.

### u16 parameter narrowing tells you the original type  <!-- id: param-narrowing -->

- A `u16` param makes MWCC insert `lsls rN,rN,#16; lsrs rN,rN,#16` narrowing at function entry; `int` params skip it. No narrowing at entry but `ldrh` use inside → the original param was likely `int` (or the caller's header said `int`).
- Calling a `u16`-declared function with an `int` argument inserts narrowing at the call site. No narrowing in the asm → the callee's prototype used `int`.
- Tail-call wrappers must forward argument types exactly — changing `int` → `u16` inserts unwanted narrowing before the tail call.

### Switch case bodies are emitted in source order  <!-- id: switch-case-source-order -->

MWCC emits switch case code blocks in **source order**, not numeric order. Jump-table entries are always numeric, but the code they point to follows source layout — reorder the C cases to match the asm's block order. Fall-through patterns also depend on case order.

### Branch polarity reveals || vs &&  <!-- id: branch-or-vs-and -->

- `if (a || b) { body }` → `cmp a; bne body; cmp b; beq skip`
- `if (a && b) { body }` → `cmp a; beq skip; cmp b; beq skip`
The branch direction (beq vs bne after comparisons) tells you which logical operator was used; getting it wrong produces same-size code with different branch instructions.

### GF_ASSERT and if/else direction  <!-- id: gf-assert-direction -->

`GF_ASSERT(cond)` expands to `if (!cond) GF_AssertFail()` — the assert-fail path is the else branch. `cmp; beq over_assert; bl AssertFail` corresponds to `if (flag == 0) { GF_AssertFail(); }`, not `GF_ASSERT(flag != 0)` — both are logically equivalent but produce different branch polarity. Swapping which path comes first changes encoding.

### lsls/lsrs pairs are bitfield extractions  <!-- id: bitfield-lsls-lsrs -->

`lsls rN,rN,#K; lsrs rN,rN,#K` extracts the low (32-K) bits. Use a bitfield struct member (e.g. `u32 fileId : 24`) rather than `& 0x00FFFFFF` — the mask may generate `ldr + and` with a literal-pool constant instead. `(x << 8) >> 8` can also produce the pattern but may not match. Bit packing order is compiler-specific: use bitfield structs, not masks.

### Loop shape selection  <!-- id: loop-shapes -->

- `for (i = 0; i < N; i++)` may compile as test-at-bottom (do/while shape) at -O4; if the count can be zero there's an early-exit check.
- Byte-clearing loops (`strb; adds; subs; bne`) need C that puts decrement+branch at the bottom: `do { } while (--n)` vs `while (n != 0) { n--; }` produce different patterns — trial and error is sometimes required.

### cmp r4 vs cmp r0 after a parameter copy (copy propagation)  <!-- id: param-copyprop-cmp -->

When a parameter (r0) is copied to a callee-saved register (`adds r4, r0, #0`), MWCC copy-propagates: comparisons on the copy are substituted back to r0. `adds r4,r0,#0; cmp r4,#N` ONLY occurs when r0 is a **function return value** saved before a later call would clobber it. If the target asm shows the cmp-on-copy pattern at function entry with no preceding bl, pure C cannot produce it — use NONMATCHING (seen in unk_0200B150.s OamManager_Create).

### Other known difficult patterns  <!-- id: misc-difficult-patterns -->

- Nested struct initialization may need exact field ordering to match.
- Inline functions from headers must match exactly as the compiler would expand them (e.g. MI_CpuClearFast/MI_CpuCopyFast wrappers inline into MIi_* tail calls — call the wrapper, not MIi_* directly).
- Functions with a `_` prefix are often compiler-generated or SDK functions (`_s32_div_f`).

### Force a jump table: list ALL dense cases explicitly (sparse -> if-else)  <!-- id: switch-jumptable-density -->

When the asm uses a Thumb jump table (cmp rN,#max; bhi default; add rN,rN; add rN,pc; ldrh [rN,#6]; add pc,rN; then a halfword offset table), the C switch must cover the range 0..max DENSELY. Listing only the cases with bodies (e.g. case 1, case 4) plus default makes MWCC emit an if-else comparison chain instead (shorter, wrong). Fix: list EVERY case 0..max explicitly, giving the empty ones a bare break (case 0: break; case 2: break; ...). MWCC then sees a dense 0..max switch and emits the jump table. Body blocks are emitted in source order, so order the non-empty cases to match the asm block layout. Diagnose via objdiff --disasm (if-else cmp chain vs add pc,rN). Note: objdiff may report a spurious SIZE diff on a matching jump-table function because it disassembles the data-region table as code ($d/$t mapping symbols differ) — confirm with chiri pkg -- compare.

### Hoist a reused computed size into a local so it lives in a callee-saved register  <!-- id: hoist-size-local-callee-saved -->

When the asm computes a value once (e.g. count*4 via a single lsls) and keeps it in a callee-saved register (r4-r7) across multiple calls that reuse it (Heap_Alloc size AND FS_ReadFile len), the source declared an explicit local for it. Recomputing inline (header.a*4 written at each Heap_Alloc/FS_ReadFile site) makes MWCC reload+recompute each time -> function grows (asm 164B, naive C 170B) and the value never occupies a persistent callee-saved reg. Fix: u32 sizeA = header.a*4; pass sizeA to both the alloc and the read. Diagnose via objdiff size diff + extra ldrh/lsls before each use. Reg pick (r6 vs r4) follows usual decl-order/param-reuse: a dead param register (path in r4) is reused for the later-born size local. Example: overlay_01_021EA6C4 ov01_021EA73C.

### Force an unsigned loop branch (bcc/blo) with a 2u literal, keeping the counter int  <!-- id: unsigned-literal-branch-no-regshuffle -->

When a loop counter is int but the asm uses an UNSIGNED branch (bcc/blo) for its bound check (cmp #N; bcc), changing the counter type to u32 fixes the branch BUT can shuffle the whole functions register allocation (u32 changes how MWCC allocates the counter and dependent temps). Instead keep the counter as int and make ONLY the comparison unsigned with an unsigned literal: for (i = 0; i < 2u; i++). The int->unsigned promotion at the compare site flips blt->bcc with zero extra instructions and leaves register allocation identical to the int version. Use this when the int version matched everything EXCEPT signed-vs-unsigned loop branches. Example: overlay_80_022384D8 ov80_0223857C (2x2 fill loops).

### Force MWCC to batch field loads before arithmetic with explicit operand locals in load order  <!-- id: explicit-operand-locals-force-load-batching -->

When a function reads several struct fields then does arithmetic on them (e.g. a point-in-rect test computing right=x+width-1, bottom=y+height-1), MWCC -O4,p's scheduler chooses whether to BATCH all the loads up front or INTERLEAVE load-compute-load-compute. Writing `int right = zone->x + zone->width - 1; int bottom = zone->y + zone->height - 1;` (named result locals, or fully-inline exprs) made MWCC compute right completely (load x, load width, add, sub) BEFORE loading y/height -> a same-SIZE-but-byte-different mismatch plus a consistent rN<->rM swap (right/y landed in swapped registers). The original loaded ALL four fields first (x, width, y, height) then did both adds then both subs. Fix: introduce one explicit local PER OPERAND, declared in the asm's load order, assigned before any use: `int x=zone->x; int width=zone->width; int y=zone->y; int height=zone->height; int right=x+width-1; int bottom=y+height-1;`. The upfront assignments make the scheduler emit the 4 loads consecutively (decl order = load order x,width,y,height) and the operand-reuse registers fall out exactly (x=r5, right=r3 reusing width's reg, y=r4, bottom=r2 reusing height's reg). Diagnose via objdiff --disasm: identical instructions/branches, only load positions + 2 cmp operand regs differ. Example: overlay_01_021FB368 ov01_021FB368 (static rect-contains helper).

### Chained field assignment stores RIGHT-first; add a local to stop a struct-store alias reload  <!-- id: chained-assign-store-order-and-alias-reload -->

Two related store/CSE tricks seen in overlay_01_021FCD2C ov01_021FCD2C. (1) STORE ORDER of a chained assignment a = b = expr: MWCC evaluates expr once, assigns to the RIGHTMOST target first, then propagates left. So `work->unk10 = work->unk20 = X;` stores unk20 THEN unk10. If the asm stores the lower offset first (str r0,[r4,#0x10] then str r0,[r4,#0x20]), you must write the chain the other way: `work->unk20 = work->unk10 = X;` (rightmost = unk10 stored first, then unk20). Diagnose via objdiff --disasm: two adjacent str of the same reg with swapped offsets. (2) ALIAS RELOAD: `work->ptrField = obj->field; ... f(obj->field);` made MWCC RELOAD obj->field for the call because the intervening store to work->ptrField may alias obj->field (it cannot prove work != obj) -> an extra ldr (SIZE +2). The asm loaded obj->field ONCE into a reg, stored it, and reused that reg for the call. Fix: hoist into an explicit local: `Camera *camera = obj->field; work->ptrField = camera; f(camera);` -> single load, register reused, no reload. The local lives in a caller-saved reg (dies after the call) so it adds no push.

### Stack-slot OFFSET assignment is reverse declaration order (first-declared = highest sp+offset)  <!-- id: stack-slot-reverse-decl-order -->

Distinct from register-allocation decl-order tricks: when a function has MULTIPLE stack-resident locals (arrays or structs that must live at sp+offset, i.e. their address is taken or they're too big for a reg), MWCC -O4,p assigns the stack SLOTS in REVERSE declaration order — the FIRST-declared local gets the HIGHEST sp offset, the LAST-declared gets the lowest. Diagnose via objdiff --disasm: same instructions but `add rN, sp, #X` / `str rN, [sp,#X]` offsets are permuted between two equal-size stack locals. Fix: reorder the C declarations so the wanted layout falls out. Examples from unk_0201F990: (a) sub_0201F990 needed `s16 box[6]; VecFx32 trans; VecFx32 scale;` in that order to get scale@sp+0x10, trans@sp+0x1c, box@sp+0x28 (box first-declared -> highest). (b) sub_0201FAC8 needed `int result; u32 polyAttr; u32 begin;` to get result@sp+8 (highest), polyAttr@sp+4, begin@sp+0. Scalars that stay in registers (pointers, ints used immediately) do NOT participate — only the spilled/addressed locals do. Related but separate from [[decl-order-regalloc]] and [[regalloc-order]] which govern which REGISTER, not which stack offset.

### Reassign a dead parameter in-place to reuse its register and steer which local spills  <!-- id: reassign-dead-param-to-steer-spill -->

When several values must survive a sequence of calls and there are more survivors than callee-saved registers, MWCC -O4,p must spill some. If objdiff shows the SAME instructions but a DIFFERENT value spilled (e.g. asm computes `subs r5,r6,r5` keeping structSize in extraSize's register and spills tableSize, while your C spills structSize and keeps tableSize in a reg -> a ~2-byte size delta), steer the allocator by REUSING a now-dead parameter's storage: write `extraSize = heapSize - extraSize;` instead of introducing a fresh `u32 structSize = heapSize - extraSize;`. The in-place reassignment makes MWCC reuse extraSize's callee-saved register for the new value (matching the asm's in-place `subs`), freeing the allocator to spill the other competing long-lived local instead. Seen in overlay_01_021FC4C4 ov01_021FC4C4 ctor. Related to [[decl-order-regalloc]] but the lever here is operand identity (reuse vs new variable), not declaration order.

### Cast index to (u32) in a GF_ASSERT range check to get the asm's unsigned (bcc/blo) compare  <!-- id: unsigned-cast-range-assert -->

Range-check asserts like `GF_ASSERT(idx < N)` (e.g. before a table lookup) compile to a SIGNED compare (cmp; blt/bge) when idx is `int`, but MWCC's array-bounds idiom in the retail code uses an UNSIGNED compare (cmp rN,#N; bcc/blo). objdiff shows a single conditional-branch opcode diff: asm `bcc/blo` (0xd3.. / unsigned-lower) vs C `blt` (0xdb.. / signed-less). Fix: cast the index to unsigned in the assert -> `GF_ASSERT((u32)idx < N);` -> emits cmp; bcc. The table index access itself (table[idx]) is unaffected by the cast. Seen across the lookup fns of unk_02077678 (sub_02077678/0207769C/02077800/02077818). Header may force the param to stay `int`, so cast at the comparison rather than changing the param type.

### Don't cache base->ptr in a local when the asm RELOADS it across calls (inverse of hoist-size-local)  <!-- id: no-cache-reloaded-pointer-across-calls -->

Counterpart to [[hoist-size-local-callee-saved]]. When a function holds a base pointer (e.g. fieldSystem in r4) and repeatedly dereferences base->ptr->field across several bl calls, MWCC RELOADS base->ptr after each call because a call may invalidate that memory (it can't prove base->ptr is unchanged). The original source therefore accessed base->ptr->field INLINE each time. Introducing a readability local `T *p = base->ptr;` breaks the match: a local is NOT invalidated by calls, so MWCC keeps it live in a CALLEE-SAVED register across the whole function, which (a) consumes an extra callee-saved reg and (b) WIDENS the push/pop (e.g. asm `push {r4,lr}` becomes C `push {r3,r4,r5,lr}`) — and the base pointer it displaces gets its own reg too. Diagnose via objdiff: many 'real byte diffs' that are actually just the wider push/pop + shifted reg numbers, and a SIZE delta of a few bytes. Fix: delete the local, write base->ptr->field inline at every use; CSE still collapses multiple derefs WITHIN a call-free span into one load (matching the asm's per-region single reload). Seen in overlay_01_021F3D38.c (ov01_021F3E10, ov01_021F3E4C: fieldSystem->unk68 reloaded 2-3x across BgSetPos/sub_0205B63C/sub_0205B6A0 calls). Contrast: cache the pointer in a local ONLY when the asm keeps it in a callee-saved reg across calls (D98 in the same file DOES cache fieldSystem->unk68 because fieldSystem itself is dead after the first load).

### Force a dedicated `sub sp` frame slot by making a small discarded-read local >4 bytes  <!-- id: force-frame-slot-oversized-discarded-local -->

When a function reads a value into a stack local that is then discarded, and the asm reserves a DEDICATED frame slot for it (prologue is `push {r3,...}` for 8-byte alignment AND a separate `sub sp,#8`, with the local accessed at `sp+0`), a scalar or any <=4-byte local does NOT match: MWCC -O4,p coalesces an address-taken local of <=4 bytes into the spare 4-byte alignment-push slot (the dummy r3 in `push {r3,r4,r5,lr}`), emitting NO `sub sp`. The function comes out 4 bytes too small (objdiff SIZE -4; prologue missing `sub sp,#N`; the rest of the body is byte-identical modulo bl placeholders). Even a 4-byte array (`u8 buf[4]`) still coalesces. FIX: declare the local LARGER than 4 bytes so it cannot fit the push slot, forcing `sub sp,#8` with the local at sp+0 — e.g. `u32 magic[2];` and read into it `NARC_ReadFile(narc, 4, magic);` (keep the read SIZE operand a literal so it is unchanged; do not use sizeof which would change #4 to #8). Seen in overlay_01_021FB04C ov01_021FB04C (discarded 4-byte NARC archive-header magic before six 2-byte count reads). Related to [[stack-slot-reverse-decl-order]] (which governs ordering of multiple stack slots) but the lever here is the local's SIZE forcing a slot to exist at all.

### Frozen struct field is s16 but asm reads ldrh: cast (u16)field  <!-- id: cast-u16-for-ldrh-on-signed-field -->

When a frozen shared struct declares a field as s16 (e.g. COORD_EVENT.x/.z in map_events_internal.h) but the target asm reads it with ldrh (unsigned, zero-extend) rather than ldrsh, don't change the shared struct (IPA risk + may be right for other files). Instead write (u16)event->field at the read site: MWCC emits a single ldrh for (u16)(s16 lvalue) (low halfword, zero-extended), matching. Plain event->field on an s16 emits ldrsh. Diagnose: objdiff/disasm shows ldrsh where retail has ldrh, often with a following sign/zero-extend mismatch. Example: src/unk_0203DB6C.c sub_0203DE04 comparing player coords (int, from u32 getters) against COORD_EVENT x/z+w/h. Note signed-vs-unsigned of the OTHER operand still controls blt vs blo: here player coords held as int and (u16)field promotes to positive int, so cmp + blt (signed). Related: [[enum-casts]].

### In a clamp/limit if-else, the NON-clamping (pass-through) arm is the if-true (fall-through) block  <!-- id: clamp-ifelse-fallthrough-arm -->

A frame-advance / clamp helper with shape `if (cond) { x = limit; flag = 1; } else { x += step; }` can match the BODY byte-for-byte yet lay the two arms out in the wrong order. The asm reveals which arm falls through: e.g. `adds r1,r3,r1; cmp r1,r4; bge CLAMP; str r1 (x+=step); b END; CLAMP: str r4 (=limit); movs r2,#1`. Here the branch (`bge`/`bmi`) targets the CLAMP block and the pass-through `str r1` is the FALL-THROUGH — so the source wrote the pass-through case as the IF-TRUE block: `if (x+step < limit) { x += step; } else { x = limit; flag = 1; }` (positive dir) and `if (x+step >= 0) { x += step; } else { x = 0; flag = 1; }` (negative dir). Writing it the intuitive way (`if (x+step >= limit) { clamp }`) inverts the polarity: MWCC emits `blt ELSE` with the clamp as fall-through — same total size but a 2-byte-shorter function and swapped bcc/blt opcodes (objdiff: N real byte diffs, function -2 bytes, but `0` flag-store reuse via movs still works). Fix: negate the condition so the asm fall-through arm is your `if` body. Seen in unk_02018000 sub_0201815C. Related: [[branch-or-vs-and]], [[gf-assert-direction]] (all about branch polarity / which path is laid out first).

### A local struct zeroed then passed by address: use aggregate-init `T x = {0,...}` (base-register stores reused for the call), not field-by-field assignment (sp-direct stores)  <!-- id: zero-struct-passed-by-addr-use-aggregate-init -->

When a function zeroes a small stack struct (e.g. VecFx32) and immediately passes its address to a callee, the retail build computes the struct address ONCE into a register (`add r1,sp,#off`), stores the zeros THROUGH that register (`str r0,[r1]; str r0,[r1,#4]; str r0,[r1,#8]`), and reuses r1 as the call's pointer arg. Writing the zero-init field-by-field (`v.x=0; v.y=0; v.z=0;`) — or even via an explicit `T *p=&v; p->x=0;...` (MWCC folds p back to the constant address) — instead emits sp-DIRECT stores (`str r0,[sp,#off]`) plus a separate `add` for the call arg. Same byte SIZE (it's a scheduling tie) but different bytes. FIX: use an aggregate initializer `VecFx32 zero = {0, 0, 0};` then `f(work, &zero);`. MWCC lowers the whole-object initializer as base-register stores and keeps the address live for the call, matching. Seen in unk_020689C8 sub_02068A08 (the else branch that supplies a zero position to sub_02068DA8). Related: [[chained-assign-store-order-and-alias-reload]].

### Overworld 2D geometry uses the XZ plane (Y is up), not XY  <!-- id: overworld-geometry-xz-plane -->

For overworld vector math (angle-between, point-to-line, segment intersection on the ground), the '2D' computation uses the .x and .z components of VecFx32, not .x and .y. Y is the up axis. In CalcAngleBetweenVecs (unk_02020B8C.s) the matching dot/cross are dot = FX_Mul(na.z,nb.z)+FX_Mul(na.x,nb.x) and cross = FX_Mul(na.z,nb.x)-FX_Mul(na.x,nb.z) (note the .z lead term and the XZ-handed cross sign, which is the negation of a naive y->z substitution). If a vec-math function diffs only in the ldr stack offsets (e.g. reading sp+44/sp+32 where you read sp+40/sp+28), suspect a .y<->.z field swap. Symptom: identical _ll_mul structure, only 4 load-offset bytes differ.

### Use a switch (shared cases) to stop MWCC fusing `x==c1 || x==c2` into a (unsigned)(x-c1)<=N range check  <!-- id: switch-form-avoids-equality-or-range-opt -->

MWCC -O4,p compiles `if (x == 2 || x == 3)` (consecutive constants) into a RANGE check: `subs rN,#2; cmp rN,#1; bhi` (or `adds #0xfe; lsls#24; lsrs#24; cmp #1; bhi` for a u8). If the target asm instead does EXPLICIT compares `cmp #2; beq IN; cmp #3; bne OUT` (the literal `||` short-circuit, no subtract/mask), rewrite the C as a switch with shared cases: `switch (x) { case 2: case 3: <body>; break; }` (for a value, `case 2: case 3: return TRUE;` then `return FALSE;`). MWCC emits the shared-case body via the same beq/bne fall-through as the `||`, but does NOT apply the range peephole — giving the exact `cmp #2; beq; cmp #3; bne` the asm has. Verified in overlay_80_02238034: BattleArcade_MultiplayerCheck (was 14 bytes range-opt -> 16 bytes explicit, matched) and the inline `ctx->type == 2 || ctx->type == 3` block guard in BattleArcade_NewBattleSetup. Diagnose: objdiff/disasm shows `subs;cmp;bhi` (C) vs `cmp;beq;cmp;bne` (asm), function 2 bytes too small. Related: [[branch-or-vs-and]], [[switch-jumptable-density]].

### VRAM key->address `(key<<16)>>13` IS NNS_GfdGetTexKeyAddr/PlttKeyAddr `((0xFFFF&key)<<3)`  <!-- id: nns-gfd-keyaddr-macro-gives-lsl16-lsr13 -->

When a function returns `lsl rN,#16; lsr rN,#13` applied to an NNSGfdTexKey/NNSGfdPlttKey (from NNS_GfdDefaultFuncAllocTexVram/PlttVram), that is the library inline NNS_GfdGetTexKeyAddr(key)/NNS_GfdGetPlttKeyAddr(key) = `(u32)((0x0000FFFF & key) << NNS_GFD_*KEY_ADDR_SHIFT)` (SHIFT=3). MWCC fuses the mask+shift `(x&0xFFFF)<<3` into `lsl#16; lsr#13`. Use the macro (include nnsys/gfd.h), not a hand-written shift. Also: a 16-bit `enum HeapID` stored in a u16 struct field (strh/ldrh) must be cast `(enum HeapID)field` at each use (MWCC errors on implicit u16->enum); the cast is free (ldrh already zero-extends). And `(NarcId)0xNN` for a literal NarcId arg. Seen in overlay_80_02239960 ov80_02239AB0/AD4 (SPLEmitter particle manager).

### Match double-math (_dflt/_dadd/_dmul/_dfix) by writing the exact decimal literal and (double) casts in evaluation order  <!-- id: double-literal-and-dflt-dmul-sequence -->

A function calling _dflt/_dadd/_dmul/_dfix is doing double-precision arithmetic on ints. Decode the double constant from its two pool words (high,low) with python struct.unpack('>d', bytes.fromhex(HItHEN LO)) -> e.g. 0x40C19999_9999999A = 9011.2. Write that exact decimal literal in C; MWCC re-encodes it to the same 64-bit pattern. `_dflt(x)` = `(double)x`, `_dfix(d)` = `(int)d`. Operand order follows source: `_dmul(a,b)` with a in (r0,r1) means `a*b`; `_dadd(CONST, y)` with the const loaded into (r0,r1) AFTER y is computed means `CONST + y` (MWCC evaluates the cheap const operand last but keeps it as the left operand). Verified: overlay_01_021F3378 ov01_021F33B8/348C matched on the FIRST build with `position.y = (int)((double)counter * (9011.2 + (double)(counter << 11)))`. Also `counter % 2` for the `lsr#31; lsl#31; sub; ror#31; add` idiom (signed mod-2). The jump-table function in the same file is an objdiff SIZE false positive ([[objdiff-false-positive-inline-jumptable-reloc]]) -- confirm with chiri pkg -- compare.

### Task/state-machine fns: break to ONE trailing `return FALSE` for a shared return-0 epilogue; keep `return TRUE` inline  <!-- id: state-machine-break-shared-return -->

A switch(state) task fn where every non-terminal case ends return FALSE and one case ends return TRUE: writing `return FALSE;` per case makes MWCC emit a separate movs r0,#0; pop for each. Retail has ONE shared return-0 block at the tail reached by branches, only return TRUE inline. Reproduce with `break;` for every FALSE path (set next state then break) and a single `return FALSE;` after the switch; keep `return TRUE;` inline. case-0 still falls through to case-1 (no break). Seen in unk_02068FC8 sub_02069498.

## IPA (-ipa file) Behavior

### Shared-header signatures are load-bearing across compilation units  <!-- id: ipa-shared-headers -->

MWCC `-ipa file` analyzes at file scope: changing a function's return or parameter types in a shared header causes cascading codegen changes in ALL functions in any compilation unit that calls it — even callers that discard the return value. If matched file A.c includes header H.h, you cannot change any declaration in H.h that A.c uses (even `void PlayBGM(u16)` → `BOOL PlayBGM(u16)`) without risking A.c's match. Workarounds: decompile header-sharing files as a group (sound.h family), fix all signatures in one coordinated commit, or NONMATCHING the conflicting functions.

### Non-static does NOT prevent IPA  <!-- id: ipa-static-no-escape -->

Making functions non-static does **not** stop `-ipa file` from optimizing across them — IPA analyzes all bodies in the compilation unit regardless of linkage. The objdump symbol table showing 'g' (global) on asm objects just means the assembler defaults labels to global, not that the original C was non-static. static vs non-static does slightly change register allocation in some cases, but never disables IPA CSE.

### IPA CSE caches repeated literal-pool addresses  <!-- id: ipa-cse-literal-pool -->

When a caller passes the same static-data address to a callee multiple times, MWCC may cache those addresses in callee-saved registers across calls, displacing other variables to the stack. The original binary may not do this if the original source structure prevented it (structure unknown). This is the blocking issue in unk_0200FA24 (BeginNormalPaletteFade calls sub_0200FE84 twice with identical pointer args).

### Frozen struct-only shared header: use a self-sufficient _internal.h in the defining TU  <!-- id: frozen-struct-header-split -->

When a save-chunk struct lives in a SHARED header frozen to struct-only (no global.h, no prototypes) so save_arrays.c stays byte-matched, that header cannot serve as the defining .c file main header: clang-format (IncludeBlocks Regroup + main-header-first) forces the same-stem header to the very top, ahead of global.h (priority 2), so u8/u16 are undefined when the struct parses. Fix: create include/<name>_internal.h that #includes global.h then re-declares the identical struct, and include THAT in the .c (its different stem dodges the main-header rule, so global.h sorts first). Leave the frozen header and save_arrays.c (DECL_CHUNK_EX) untouched; give public fns local forward declarations. Verify save_arrays.o is byte-identical (cmp) to confirm no IPA cascade. Example: unk_0202E41C.

### Use a private struct + cast when a shared param struct is incomplete (IPA-safe)  <!-- id: private-struct-for-incomplete-shared-type -->

When a function must allocate/fill a struct that an EXTERNAL matched function takes by pointer (e.g. PokeathlonCourse_LaunchApp(.., PokeathlonCourseArgs*)), but the shared struct in its header is incomplete/placeholder (filler bytes, more-fields-to-discover) and is included by other already-matched files: do NOT edit the shared header to name the fields (recompiles those TUs -> IPA cascade risk). Instead define a fully-typed PRIVATE struct in your .c with the exact byte layout you need and cast to the real type only at the external call: PokeathlonCourse_LaunchApp(fs, (PokeathlonCourseArgs *)work->app). sizeof(private)==sizeof(real) so the alloc size literal matches; field offsets you control reproduce the exact ldrb/ldrh/strb. Zero shared-header change = zero IPA risk. Example: unk_02095DF4 sub_02095E30.

### Frozen prototype header (u32 sigs, no global.h) also needs the _internal.h split  <!-- id: frozen-prototype-header-split -->

Generalizes frozen-struct-header-split to plain PROTOTYPE headers. If include/<name>.h declares the module funcs (e.g. u32 ov01_xxx(u32,u32)) but does NOT include global.h (relies on callers including global.h first), and it is included by already-matched files: when YOU write src/<name>.c, clang-format IncludeBlocks=Regroup + main-header-first force the same-stem <name>.h to the very top, ABOVE global.h. u32 is then undefined while the header parses -> MWCC treats u32 as implicit int -> later types.h redeclares u32 as unsigned long -> error: identifier u32 redeclared / function has no prototype. Fix: do NOT include the same-stem header in the .c; create include/<name>_internal.h (different stem dodges the main-header sort, sorts AFTER global.h) that #includes global.h then declares the same prototypes; include THAT. Leave the frozen <name>.h untouched so the matched callers do not recompile. Example: overlay_01_021F467C.

### Local frozen extern when a callee's header narrowed its params (int->u16) after this caller was matched  <!-- id: frozen-callee-proto-for-narrowed-args -->

Split-header discipline applies to CALLEE prototypes too, not just shared struct headers. If a function was originally compiled with a wider arg type for a callee (e.g. int) and the callee's header was LATER refined to a narrow type (u16/u8/s16), including that refined header makes MWCC emit an integer-narrowing the original asm lacks: a u32/int value passed to a u16 param gets a `lsls rN,#16; lsrs rN,#16` (zero-extend) or `lsls;asrs` (sign) truncation at the call site. Diagnose via objdiff --disasm: extra lsl/lsr #16 pairs around a bl that the asm doesn't have. Fix: do NOT include the refined header; declare a local `extern <ret> Fn(... int a2, int a3 ...);` with the wider (matched) arg types so no narrowing is emitted. Only works if the refined header is not force-included (grep its includers first; global.h chain must not pull it). Seen in unk_02097BE0 calling LegendaryCinematic_LaunchApp (launch_application.h has u16 a2/a3; matched int). Contrast [[frozen-prototype-header-split]] (struct/decl header) — same principle, applied to an imported function signature. NB: MWCC DOES narrow u32->u16 for outgoing args (confirmed: unk_020551B8 Sound_SetSceneAndPlayBGM seqNo), so a missing truncation in asm means the param was wider at match time.

### Header declares a narrower return type than the field (u8 vs u32) -> MWCC masks; if asm does not mask, the real return type is the wider one — use split-header  <!-- id: narrow-return-type-masks-split-header -->

Symptom: a getter that just does `ldr r0,[p,#off]; bx lr` (no lsl/lsr/and mask) but the existing/public header declares it returning u8 (or u16). With that header, MWCC appends a truncation (`lsls r0,#24; lsrs r0,#24`) and the function is 4 bytes too big (objdiff SIZE 10 vs 14). The asm proves the real return type is u32/int (the value is returned full-width; any narrowing is the CALLERs job). Fix WITHOUT editing the shared header (it is frozen at the matching-time state its callers were built against — changing the return type would alter caller codegen and break their match / cascade via IPA): do NOT include that public header in the defining .c. Instead include the underlying data/struct header (here friend_group.h) and forward-declare the affected functions LOCALLY with the correct (wider) return type. Different TUs may legitimately see different return-type declarations for the same symbol in a matching decomp — the linker only matches by name. Seen in unk_0202C730.c: Save_FriendGroup_GetGroupId declared u8 in unk_0202C730.h (5 matched callers) but defined u32 locally to drop the mask. Verified: full ROM SHA1 still passes, callers unaffected.

### Own-header-first + non-self-sufficient frozen header: make the .c self-contained  <!-- id: self-contained-when-own-header-not-self-sufficient -->

clang-format sorts a .c file's OWN header (matching basename, e.g. text_0205B4EC.h for src/text_0205B4EC.c) to the very top, before all other includes. If that frozen shared header is NOT self-sufficient — it uses a type it doesn't include (e.g. text_0205B4EC.h declares a fn taking FontID but only includes bg_window.h/options.h/pm_string.h, not font_types_def.h) — then including it first leaves that type undefined and MWCC mis-parses the declaration ('illegal function definition' + 'identifier redeclared' with a truncated signature + cascading 'illegal access to local variable from other function'). Other files that include the header compile only because, for THEM, it's not the main header so it sorts alphabetically AFTER something that pulls the type in (e.g. font.h). You hit this on the FIRST file decompiled from that module. Fixes: (a) add the missing include to the shared header — usually IPA-safe since every existing includer must already have the type before it, so it's a guard no-op — but it still edits a frozen header; (b) PREFERRED: make the new .c self-contained — do NOT include the shared header at all, instead write local prototypes for every function the file defines (matching the header's frozen signatures exactly for the exported ones, plus any .public fns missing from the header), and include the concrete headers that provide the called fns/types. Zero risk to other TUs; the shared header stays untouched for its callers. Example: src/text_0205B4EC.c (FontID via text_0205B4EC.h). Related: [[enum-casts]], [[frozen-struct-header-split]].

### When a frozen shared header declares cluster-partner fns with PLACEHOLDER return/param types, a client accessing fields beyond those types must declare them locally (don't include the header)  <!-- id: placeholder-header-types-need-local-redecl-for-extra-fields -->

A shared header (e.g. overlay_01_021F1348.h) sometimes declares a still-asm module's exported functions with PLACEHOLDER types that are link-correct but structurally wrong for some callers — e.g. `TaskManager *ov01_021F1468(FieldSystem*)` where the real returned struct is larger and a new client reads `ret->field@0x24` (out of bounds for TaskManager). The existing matched callers only touch the declared fields, so the placeholder works for them and the header is frozen. A NEW client that needs the extra fields canNOT include that header (the placeholder types won't compile the field access, and editing the header IPA-cascades the other callers). Fix (extends [[frozen-prototype-header-split]] / [[frozen-callee-proto-for-narrowed-args]]): do NOT include the shared header; declare the needed cluster-partner functions LOCALLY in the .c with your own accurate struct types (all pointer/int args → identical call ABI, so codegen matches), and define the structs you need locally. The linker resolves by name. Also applies to same-module accessors split across headers (e.g. sub_02068D74/D90/DA8 not in unk_020689C8.h → declare locally). Seen in overlay_01_02203E40.c (a 3D-model-on-mapobject effect): local decls for ov01_021F1430/146C/1468/1450/1620/1448/1AB8 + sub_02068D74/90/98/DA8/DB8 + VEC_MultAdd/VEC_Distance, custom UnkOv01_02203E40 object (NNSG3dRenderObj@0x4, f32 scale@0x64) and a renderer struct with Camera*@0x24. Verified full ROM SHA1 (existing header callers untouched).

### MWCC -W error rejects a non-static function definition with no prototype ("function has no prototype"); for exports kept out of a frozen header, add LOCAL prototypes in the .c  <!-- id: mwcc-requires-prototype-local-decl -->

This build uses -W error, so every non-static (exported) function needs a visible prototype before its definition. When a file exports many functions but the shared header is frozen at a subset (only the symbols matched callers use), do NOT add the rest to the header (IPA cascade into those callers).
