Instead declare the extra exports as plain (non-static) prototypes at the top of the .c itself. unk_020379A0.s exports 19 fns; include/unk_020379A0.h has 6; the other 13 got local prototypes. Codegen is identical whether the prototype lives in a header or the .c, as long as the types match. Relatedly: never mark them static (they ARE exported and other asm files call them).

### ipa-shared-headers (sound.h): pass u16 funcs as int locally when a wider value is passed  <!-- id: shared-sound-header-int-vs-u16-mask -->

The sound functions PlaySE/StopSE (unk_02005D10.h, sound.h family) are declared with u16 params in the current headers, but at matching time several callers were compiled against int-param declarations. A file that passes a WIDER value (e.g. FrontierScript_ReadVar returns u32) to PlaySE(u16) gets an MWCC truncation mask (lsls r0,#16; lsrs r0,#16) that the retail asm does NOT have - because the asm saw an int param (no conversion). Fix with the split-header pattern: do NOT include unk_02005D10.h/sound.h; declare the SE/fanfare functions locally with int params [void PlaySE(int); void StopSE(int,int); etc.]. Callers passing u16 values are unaffected (u16->int and u16->u16 both emit no mask), which is why only u32-passing files trip the gate. Note the BGM funcs (PlayBGM, Sound_SetFieldBGM) genuinely take u16 - a value passed to them DOES get masked if stored in a wider local (use u32 seqNo). Saw in overlay_80_02235390.c.

### A file gated_by ipa-shared-headers can still be decompiled if it only CALLS the shared-header functions (no signature change)  <!-- id: ipa-blocked-files-can-call-sound-fns-without-cascade -->

The ipa-shared-headers blocker (sound.h / unk_02005D10.h family) is about CHANGING a signature in a shared header, which cascades into already-matched callers. A new file that merely CALLS those functions (e.g. PlaySE/StopSE, declared in include/unk_02005D10.h) with their existing signatures needs NO header change, so there is no cascade — just #include the existing header and call them. The triage's `gated_by: ipa-shared-headers` is conservative (flags any file sharing symbols with the blocked cluster); check whether the file actually needs to ADD/CHANGE a declaration before treating it as blocked. overlay_01_021F3114 (a PlayerAvatar turn-task calling PlaySE(SEQ_SE_DP_F209)/StopSE) matched 6/6 this way.

## Data Sections

### Section ↔ C mapping  <!-- id: section-mapping -->

- `.rodata` = const arrays/tables (use `const`); `.data` = initialized mutable globals; `.bss` = zero-initialized globals.
- Global variable order matters: declarations must match the asm order, and `.rodata` array order must match the section layout (an all-functions-match file can still fail ROM SHA1 on rodata order — see unk_0201010C).
- `.balign 4, 0` pads to 4-byte boundary — use struct padding or explicit alignment.
- ARM is little-endian: `.byte 0x25, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00` = u32 `0x00000025`.

### Data-only files  <!-- id: data-only-files -->

Some asm files contain only `.rodata`/`.data` sections. They need C files with const (or non-const) arrays matching the exact byte layout:
```c
#include "global.h"

const u8 sDataTable[] = {
    0x25, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
};
```

### BSS sizing with raw byte arrays  <!-- id: bss-sizing -->

When asm BSS symbol sizes don't match `sizeof(StructType)`, use a raw `u8 array[0xNN]` and cast at usage sites: `*(StructType *)array`. Multiple BSS variables become separate `.bss` sections in the object but the linker merges them — the total size must match.

### Contiguous data arrays accessed via base+offset  <!-- id: contiguous-arrays-base-offset -->

When multiple data labels are accessed from a common base pointer (e.g. `ldr r0, =_0210F64C; str r1, [r0, #0x10]` targeting `_0210F65C`), the labels are contiguous. Declare them as separate static arrays in order — MWCC lays them out contiguously. Stores use base symbol + offset while call arguments use the target symbol directly; both produce correct literal pools as long as the arrays are separate declarations (not one big array with #defines).

### Packed lookup tables (VALUE | (code<<N)) are bitfield structs; access via members emits the asm's shift extraction  <!-- id: packed-lookup-table-is-bitfield-struct -->

A rodata table whose entries are `KEY | (CODE << N)` (e.g. `SPECIES_X | (22<<10)`) and whose readers extract fields with SHIFT PAIRS (`lsl #(32-N); lsr #(32-N)` for the low field; `lsl #16; lsr #(16+N)` style for the high field) is, in the original source, an array of a BITFIELD struct: `typedef struct { u16 key : N; u16 code : (16-N); } E;` with initializers `{ KEY, CODE }`. Accessing `tbl[i].key` / `tbl[i].code` makes MWCC emit the exact shift-pair extraction. Writing it as `static const u16 tbl[]` + `(tbl[i] & MASK)` / `(tbl[i] >> N)` instead emits AND-with-a-loaded-mask-register and asr — which (a) differ instruction-for-instruction and (b) consume an extra register for the mask, forcing a callee-saved reg + push/pop (function SIZE grows). Seen in unk_020517A4 (_020FC3B4 species table, _020FC3CA trainerclass table; both `{u16 id:10; u16 param:6}`). Diagnose: objdiff shows asr/and+mask vs lsl/lsr pairs, often with a spurious push {..} the asm lacks.

### Data-only files in a custom abs32 section with multiple ordered symbols (e.g. .version SDK version strings) have no known matching C form under MWCC sp2p2 — keep as asm  <!-- id: version-custom-section-data-unmatchable -->

asm/middleware.s is 7 NUL-terminated SDK version strings in ONE .version section (define_section VERSION ".version" abs32 RWX in <nitro/section.h>), each .balign 4, total 224 bytes, in source order. No C incantation reproduces a single ordered 4-aligned .version section: (1) bare `VERSION x[]` declspec prefix -> "declaration syntax error"; (2) `const` data IGNORES `#pragma section VERSION begin/end` and lands in the merged .rodata (correct order, packed, WRONG section); (3) NON-const data WITH the begin/end pragma reaches .version but MWCC -O4 emits each symbol as its OWN .version sub-section SORTED BY SIZE (not source order) — `__attribute__((aligned(4)))` fixes the per-object 4-byte alignment (algn 2**2) but cannot fix the order; full compare FAILs main.sbin + OVY_45.sbin. Also: objdiff.py does NOT track custom sections (it reports asm .rodata=0), so only `chiri pkg -- compare` can verify these. Verdict: defer / keep asm. Triage ranks it #1 (data-only, 36 lines) but that is a false-easy.

### MWCC -ipa file emits consecutive file-scope const STRUCTs in reverse definition order  <!-- id: mwcc-rodata-const-struct-reverse-order -->

When a file has multiple file-scope `static const` struct objects (e.g. several OverlayManagerTemplate launch templates) plus a const array (a jump/function-pointer table), MWCC -ipa file lays out .rodata with the const structs in REVERSE source-definition order, with the array kept last. Symptom: all functions match in objdiff but `main.sbin`/full ROM SHA1 FAILS, and `objdump -t -j .rodata` shows the struct objects at swapped offsets vs the asm (e.g. you defined _02108EA0 then _02108EB0 but MWCC emitted EB0@0x00, EA0@0x10). Fix: define the const structs in the OPPOSITE order to how you want them emitted (define EB0 then EA0 to get EA0@0x00, EB0@0x10). Verified in unk_02097024.c: two OverlayManagerTemplate + one state-func jump table. The jump-table array stayed last in both orderings. Always run `chiri pkg -- compare`, not just objdiff — this is a section-layout diff objdiff cannot see.

### Data file with many exported const arrays that contain RELOCATIONS (e.g. function pointers): MWCC -ipa file emits one .rodata section per symbol, grouped by size and PERMUTED within each size-group by a fixed positional permutation. Reorder the source to invert it.  <!-- id: exported-const-fnptr-array-section-reorder -->

scrcmd_mart-style const arrays of plain immediates (ITEM_*, no relocations) stay in source order and match. But exported const arrays that hold cross-TU symbol refs (function-pointer step tables like gMovementCmdSteps_NNN -> MapObjectMovementCmd*_Step*) are emitted by MWCC as one separate .rodata section EACH, then ordered: first bucketed by section size (all 8-byte arrays, then all 0xc-byte arrays, ...), and within each bucket permuted by a fixed positional permutation Q that depends only on the count, NOT on the names/content. The linker preserves the .o section order, so a per-symbol objdiff PASSES while `chiri pkg -- compare` FAILS on rodata order (cf the unk_0201010C warning). RECIPE to match: (1) write arrays in asm-label order and build; (2) read the placed order `O = objdump -t obj.o | grep 'O .rodata' | awk '{print $NF}'`; (3) for each source index i, Q[i] = index of asmOrder[i] within O; (4) rewrite the source definitions as S[i] = asmOrder[Q[i]]; rebuild and confirm objdump order == asm order, then `chiri pkg -- compare`. Verified on unk_data_020FD978 (17 arrays: 8-byte Q=[2,3,0,4,5,1,9,8,7,6], 0xc-byte Q=[0,1,3,4,2,5,6]). The source ends up in a non-obvious order; that's expected and load-bearing. See [[section-mapping]].

## Recurring File/Module Patterns

### Task callback pattern (field system)  <!-- id: task-callback-pattern -->

1. A public `sub_XXXX` allocates a work struct via `Heap_AllocAtEnd`, fills it, calls `TaskManager_Call(man, callback, env)`.
2. A static callback uses `TaskManager_GetFieldSystem` + `TaskManager_GetEnvironment`, implements a state machine (switch on `env->state`), returns TRUE when done after `Heap_Free`.
- The callback is referenced by literal pool (`_XXXX: .word sub_YYYY`) in the caller.
- Work struct fields can be inferred from how the caller stores arguments and the callback reads offsets.

### Save chunk pattern  <!-- id: save-chunk-pattern -->

1. `sub_XXXX_sizeof(void)` returns `sizeof(StructType)` — trivial.
2. `sub_XXXX_init(StructType *a0)` clears with `MI_CpuClear32`/`MI_CpuClear8` then sets defaults.
3. A getter calls `SaveArray_Get(saveData, SAVE_INDEX)` and returns the pointer; field getters/setters are trivial.
- `save_arrays.c` registers these via `DECL_CHUNK_EX` — replace the macro with an `#include` of the new header and remove the `DECL_CHUNK_EX` line. Check the index in `include/constants/save_arrays.h`.

### Overlay specifics  <!-- id: overlay-notes -->

- Overlay functions are named `ovNN_XXXXXXXX` (NN = overlay number, XXXXXXXX = address); overlay code loads at specific VMAs visible in labels.
- Overlay dependencies are declared in main.lsf (`After` clauses); each overlay has its own .sbin SHA1.

### Public vs static visibility  <!-- id: public-vs-static -->

Always check `asm/include/<file>.inc` `.public` declarations before marking functions static. Public functions must NOT be static (overlays call static-module functions by name → linker Undefined errors otherwise) and belong in `include/<file>.h`. The `.public` list mixes exports and imports — cross-reference with `thumb_func_start`/`arm_func_start` to split them.

### Enum casts required by -W noimplicitconv  <!-- id: enum-casts -->

MWCC rejects implicit int→enum conversions:
- `NarcId`: `GfGfxLoader_LoadCharData((NarcId)0x26, ...)`
- `GFPalSlotOffset`: cast computed expressions like `(enum GFPalSlotOffset)(palette_num << 5)`
- Any computed integer passed to an enum parameter needs an explicit cast.

### Save-chunk decomp IPA-safe: dedicated header, LEAVE save_arrays.c DECL_CHUNK_EX  <!-- id: save-chunk-ipa-safe -->

To decompile a save-chunk module (SaveArray_Get + MIi_CpuClear32, sizeof/init + field accessors) without IPA cascade: (1) put the struct + all prototypes in a NEW dedicated include/<name>.h that ONLY the new .c includes. (2) DO NOT modify save_arrays.c — leave its DECL_CHUNK_EX(sizefn, initfn) macro in place. Replacing the macro with #include <name>.h (the old pre-IPA-discipline move) recompiles save_arrays.c against a changed header set and IPA-cascades its codegen -> ROM mismatch. The DECL_CHUNK_EX extern decls and the new header decls coexist fine (separate TUs). sizeof fn: return sizeof(Struct); init: MI_CpuClear32(ptr, <sizeoffn>()) then set defaults; getter: return SaveArray_Get(saveData, SAVE_UNK_NN). Verify with chiri pkg -- compare (objdiff bl-placeholder diffs on the init are benign). Supersedes the earlier save-chunk-pattern that said to replace the macro.

### sub_0203410C command-table registrar files (e.g. unk_02091564.c, unk_0208F658.c): a .rodata table of {handler, sizeGetter, recordGetter} triples registered by a tail-call to sub_0203410C(&table, NELEMS, arg)  <!-- id: sub_0203410C-command-table-family -->

A recurring module shape: an exported registrar `void reg(void *arg){ sub_0203410C(&sTable, NELEMS(sTable), arg); }` that TAIL-CALLs sub_0203410C (loads addr, `bx r3`, since the callee is far). The .rodata `sTable[]` is N triples; columns are func1 = `void handler(int a0, int a1, void *a2, ctx *a3)` (dispatched by sub_02034170 with a3 = (*globalCtx)->field8 or NULL), func2 = `u32 sizeGetter(void)` (commonly sub_020342C4/020342C0 returning 0xFFFF/0), func3 = `void *recordGetter(int idx, ctx *a3)` or NULL. In the handlers, `a0` is a link/player id compared against `sub_0203769C()` for an early return; `a3->0xc` is a `SaveData*`, `a3->0x88` is a per-category mixing buffer (set by a sibling setter that does `*(void**)((u8*)a3+0x88)=buf`). Define a file-local struct typedef for the table (exact func-ptr types) instead of reusing UnkStruct_02091564 to avoid func3 return-type (void* vs void(*)()) warnings — rodata bytes are identical either way. Access the big buffer via raw `*(T*)((u8*)buf+off)` casts. (template: src/unk_02091564.c)

## NONMATCHING Fallback

### NONMATCHING inline asm syntax (MWCC)  <!-- id: nonmatching-inline-asm-syntax -->

When using `asm void FuncName(...)`:
- `ldr rN, =0xVALUE` for literal-pool constants (NOT `ldr rN, label` + `label: .word`); `ldr rN, =FuncName` for function pointers.
- `bl FuncName` works directly; local labels (`_0201013A:`) work for branches.
- `.balign` directives are NOT supported — remove them.
- Wrap in `// clang-format off` / `// clang-format on`, and gate the C version with `#ifdef NONMATCHING`.

### MWCC collapses a deliberately-redundant double zero-load; NONMATCHING after a couple tries  <!-- id: redundant-double-zero-load-coalesce-wall -->

Some asm loads the SAME constant 0 into two registers (e.g. a byte-clear fill in caller-saved r1 + a separate i/state 0 in callee-saved r4), i.e. it is LESS optimal than necessary. Pure C re-converges: MWCC -O4 constant-coalesces the two zeros into one callee-saved register (the fill merges into i), producing one fewer movs -> a 2-byte SIZE diff. Source tricks that do NOT break the coalesce: block-scoping the clear, a named u8 fill var, tying state=i (manager->state = i; for(;i<2;i++)), C99 for-scoped i, do-while vs for. If you see a function that is identical except the asm has an extra movs #0 (redundant constant load) that your C optimizes away, do not burn many build cycles -- NONMATCHING that one function (asm static, keep C under ifdef NONMATCHING) and move on. Example: overlay_01_021FB4C0 ov01_021FB55C (struct byte-clear + slot-init).

### NONMATCHING inline asm: declare compiler-runtime callees as extern, and use explicit [rN, #0] (bracket-only assembles wrong)  <!-- id: nonmatching-inline-asm-mwasmarm-gotchas -->

Two mwasmarm gotchas when transcribing a function to MWCC inline asm (`static asm void f(...) { ... }`) for a NONMATCHING fallback: (1) `bl _s32_div_f` (or any compiler-runtime/IPA helper: _s32_div_f, _ll_mul, _u32_div_f, etc.) fails to assemble with `undefined label`. Fix: add a C prototype before the function so the symbol is known to the linker — e.g. `extern int _s32_div_f(int numer, int denom);`. Named callees that are already declared (your own sub_*, SDK fns) work directly. (2) Bracket-only load/store addressing assembles with a WRONG offset: `ldr r2, [r5]` came out as `ldr r2, [r5, #8]` (one stray instruction, objdiff 1 real byte diff at that halfword). Always write the explicit zero offset: `ldr r2, [r5, #0]`. (Curiously `strh r0, [r4]` assembled fine as [r4,#0] in the same function, so it is inconsistent — just always write #0.) Literal loads: use `ldr rN, =0xVALUE`; mwasmarm auto-dumps the pool at function end in first-use order with dedup (matched the retail pool 0x798/0x78c/0x60c/0x78d exactly). bl placeholders match the original asm .o byte-for-byte (both assembled by mwasmarm), so objdiff shows them as benign BL-reloc diffs, not real diffs. Wrap the body in // clang-format off/on and gate the readable C under #ifdef NONMATCHING. Seen in unk_02014A08 sub_02014CBC. Related: [[nonmatching-inline-asm-syntax]].

### MWCC fills a load-use delay slot with an independent extraction; retail does not — same instrs, reordered, often unmatchable from C  <!-- id: load-delay-slot-fill-scheduling-resists-c -->

After a load (e.g. `ldrsh sine`), MWCC -O4,p schedules an INDEPENDENT ready instruction into the 1-cycle load-use delay slot to avoid a stall — typically a halfword extraction from a still-live value (e.g. `lsrs hi, v, #16`). The retail build sometimes does NOT do this fill (it issues the dependent op immediately, accepting the stall). The two builds then have IDENTICAL instructions in a DIFFERENT order (objdiff: same SIZE, N real byte diffs that are all reordered shifts/extractions, no opcode changes). This ordering is the scheduler reacting to the IR shape; it resists C-level control. Tried (unk_02014A08 sub_02014CBC, packing `(hi<<16)|(u16)newLow` where hi=(u16)(v>>16)): inline vs separate temp, `u16 hi` vs inline cast, `(v>>16)<<16` (becomes AND-mask + literal), in-place `v>>=16;v<<=16` (folds to AND-mask), and OR-operand swap. The operand swap `(u16)newLow | ((u16)(v>>16)<<16)` got CLOSEST (20->9 diffs) but never to 0 — MWCC kept slotting the hi-extract before newLow. When a same-size all-reordered-instruction diff survives ~4-5 expression rewrites, stop and NONMATCHING (the asm transcribes cleanly: 18/19 other fns stayed clean C). Related: [[redundant-double-zero-load-coalesce-wall]], [[nonmatching-inline-asm-mwasmarm-gotchas]].

### Single-TU split-param (u8 stack arg) and a computed-reduction spill in the lowest slot can be unmatchable -> NONMATCHING  <!-- id: single-tu-split-param-and-reduction-spill-nonmatching -->

Two MWCC register-allocator behaviors that resist source control within ONE translation unit: (1) Split-param: a callee reads a u8 STACK param via ldrb (no narrow) while the retail caller passes the int with no narrow; with caller+callee in the SAME TU there is one prototype — u8 makes the caller narrow (lsls#24/lsrs#24 before the stack store), int makes the callee narrow for its bitfield/compare. The split-header trick (different prototype per file) does not apply. (2) A computed reduction temp (sum of several already-spilled values) can be assigned the LOWEST spill slot (sp+0x20) instead of its computation-order slot, shifting every earlier spill by +4 — not fixable by declaration order, by moving the decl, or by extracting the embedded call. When both hit one large function, wrap it as `asm` NONMATCHING and keep the file's other functions as matching C (the ROM still matches). Seen in unk_02068FC8 sub_02068FC8 (a1 stack param to sub_02069308; the `sum` GameStats reduction).

### MWCC inline `asm` quirks: bare [rN] memory operands misassemble — use [rN, #0]; encode jump-table halfwords as `lsl rd,rm,#0`  <!-- id: mwcc-inline-asm-needs-explicit-zero-offset-and-lsl-jumptable -->

Writing a NONMATCHING `asm static void f(...) {...}` block in MWCC sp2p2: (1) A bare memory operand `ldr r0, [r3]` (no offset) misassembles (observed as `ldr r0,[r3,#8]`); ALWAYS write the explicit offset `ldr r0, [r3, #0]` / `str r0, [r4, #0]`. (2) `movs rd, rm` is rejected (parsed as a label → 'unknown assembler instruction mnemonic' / 'label movs redefined'); use `lsl rd, rm, #0` instead. (3) For a Thumb `add pc, rN` jump table, MWCC inline asm does NOT support `.short label-label-2` data directives — encode each jump-table halfword as a `lsl rd, rm, #0` instruction whose machine encoding equals the offset (lsl rd,rm,#0 = 0x0000|(rm<<3)|rd, e.g. 0x0006=`lsl r6,r0,#0`, 0x0012=`lsl r2,r2,#0`, 0x000a=`lsl r2,r1,#0`, 0x0010=`lsl r0,r2,#0`), per src/battle/battle_hp_bar.c. (4) `ldr rN, =symbol` and `ldr rN, =0xVALUE` work; `bl FuncName` to externs/statics works; `.balign` is unsupported. Diagnose a wrong NONMATCHING result by disassembling the built .o (objdump) and byte-comparing; objdiff's per-function SIZE for a jump-table fn is unreliable (data-region $d/$t mapping) — confirm with chiri pkg -- compare. Used to NONMATCHING ov01_02200A08 (camera-family render cb, MWCC list-scheduler tie-break on the scale-copy temp registers).

## Tooling & Build Workflow

### objdiff.py usage and reliability  <!-- id: objdiff-usage -->

```bash
cp build/heartgold.us/asm/foo.o /tmp/foo_asm.o   # before flipping main.lsf
python3 tools/decomp_harness/objdiff.py /tmp/foo_asm.o build/heartgold.us/src/foo.o
python3 tools/decomp_harness/objdiff.py ... --summary      # also checks .rodata/.data/.bss
python3 tools/decomp_harness/objdiff.py ... --bytes sub_X  # per-function byte diff
```
- Plain function MATCH is based on **size**, not bytes — same-size functions with different registers report as MATCH. Verify critical functions with `--disasm FN`/`--bytes FN`.
- `--summary` checks data sections too; use it when pre-existing build errors block full-ROM `make compare`.

### Build workflow on macOS  <!-- id: build-macos -->

- Always `chiri pkg -- build` (or `-- compare`), never raw `make -C` — Wine CWD resolution breaks through symlinks and `.d` files get stale `Z:` paths (make spins at 100% CPU).
- Fast iteration: `chiri pkg -- build --target main --no-compare` (ARM9 only), then `chiri pkg -- compare`.
- Corrupted `.d` files: `find build -name "*.d" -delete` then `chiri pkg -- tidy` and rebuild.
- Prerequisites: `brew install gnu-sed arm-gcc-bin` (osx-cross/homebrew-arm tap).

### recomp.sh build recovery  <!-- id: recomp-tool -->

`./tools/decomp_harness/recomp.sh` handles build recovery: `--kill` (stale make/wine/mwcc), `--fix-d` (corrupted .d files), `--full` (clean rebuild), no args = kill + fix .d + tidy + rebuild main. Use when builds hang at 100% CPU, error after an asm→C switch in main.lsf, or won't restart after an interrupt.

### Verify a single object when the full build is blocked  <!-- id: single-object-build-escape -->

When an unrelated pre-existing error aborts make main (e.g. a dup-decl in a shared header), you can still compile+verify ONE file: cp the asm reference first (build/heartgold.us/asm/<name>.o to /tmp), switch main.lsf, then build just that object via the chiri make-target passthrough: chiri pkg -- build --no-compare -- build/heartgold.us/src/<name>.o (default --target all => empty make target, so the bare object path is the only thing built). Then objdiff.py --summary /tmp/<name>_asm.o build/heartgold.us/src/<name>.o. Isolates your file from the broken TU; gives function+data .o-level verification without the full ROM SHA1.

### objdiff bl-placeholder diffs are benign; chiri pkg -- compare is authoritative  <!-- id: objdiff-bl-placeholder-falsepos -->

objdiff.py can report DIFF on a function whose disassembly is byte-identical except the UNRELOCATED bl placeholder bytes: the assembler (mwasmarm) emits f7ff fffe for an external call, MWCC emits f000 f800. objdiff sees these as real halfword diffs (and may not pair them as bl-reloc diffs), but the linker overwrites both with the same relocated offset, so the final ROM is identical. Always confirm with chiri pkg -- compare (full ROM SHA1) before rejecting OR accepting: compare is the only authoritative test. objdiff also MISSES section-level diffs (alignment/padding/rodata). Use objdiff --disasm to confirm a flagged diff is only bl placeholders, then trust compare.

### Include NNS via global.h, never the leaf <nnsys/...> headers directly  <!-- id: nns-leaf-headers-via-global -->

NNS SDK leaf headers (e.g. <nnsys/g3d/binres/res_struct_accessor.h>, res_struct_accessor_inline.h, kernel.h, gfd VramMan types) do NOT include their own prerequisite type headers -> including them directly gives MWCC declaration syntax error (NNSG3dResMdlSet etc. undefined). The umbrella nnsys/g3d.h includes them in the correct dependency order, and global.h -> nitro/nnsys pulls the whole chain. Fix: rely on #include global.h for ALL NNS types AND inline accessors (NNS_G3dGetMdlByIdx, NNS_G3dGetResDataByIdx live in res_struct_accessor_inline.h which g3d.h includes). Do not add explicit <nnsys/...> includes; clang-format also sorts angle-bracket system includes to the TOP (above global.h), compounding the undefined-type failure. Example: unk_02069660.

### objdiff.py misreports SIZE/section for functions with inline Thumb jump-table data  <!-- id: objdiff-size-miscount-inline-jumptable -->

MWCC emits Thumb switch dispatch as `add r0,r0; add r0,pc; ldrh r0,[r0,#6]; lsl;asr; add pc,r0` followed by inline .short/.word offset-table data embedded in .text. objdiff.py's function-boundary/size heuristic can't tell this inline data from code, so it reports a spurious `SIZE N vs M` (often +8) for such functions and a small nonzero section-size delta — even when the bytes are IDENTICAL. The asm side disassembles the table as `.short`/`.word` (it has the source directives) while the C .o side shows the same bytes as bogus instructions (e.g. `movs r0,r1` = 0x0008). Verify with --disasm: if the instruction stream AND the table halfwords match (only bl relocs differ: asm fff7/feff vs c 00f0/00f8), the function matches. ALWAYS confirm with `chiri pkg -- compare` (authoritative) rather than trusting objdiff SIZE for jump-table functions. Seen in unk_02097BE0 (sub_02097BE0 5-case, sub_02097C50 4-case).

### When chiri compare fails but objdiff shows only jump-table SIZE mismatches, diff main.sbin built both ways  <!-- id: pinpoint-1byte-via-main-sbin-diff -->

For files full of inline-jump-table functions, objdiff reports SIZE mismatches for every function (it miscounts the inline .short tables) and refuses byte-level diffs, hiding any real 1-byte error. To pinpoint: build main with the C version (chiri pkg -- build --target main --no-compare) and `cp build/heartgold.us/main.sbin /tmp/main_c.sbin`; flip main.lsf back to the asm object, rebuild, `cp ... /tmp/main_asm.sbin`; then `cmp -l /tmp/main_asm.sbin /tmp/main_c.sbin` (asm baseline matches retail). cmp -l prints offsets+values in OCTAL and is 1-based. Convert: address = 0x02000000 + (byteno-1). `xxd -s <off> -l 48` both sbins to see context, then map to the function via the asm listing. This isolates a single differing byte (e.g. an asr-vs-lsr opcode) that objdiff masked. Used to find the lsr/asr bug in unk_0205BFF0 sub_0205C0A0.

### Trailing .balign 4,0 in asm inflates per-function symbol size by 2 vs MWCC; benign section -2N delta  <!-- id: balign-trailing-pad-section-size-falsepos -->

Hand-written asm functions that end on a 2-byte (Thumb) boundary often carry a trailing `.balign 4, 0` before `thumb_func_end`, which the assembler folds INTO the function symbol (size rounded up +2, padding zeros counted as part of the function). MWCC does NOT pad the tail of a function; it 4-byte-aligns the NEXT function instead, so the same 2 bytes of zero padding exist between functions but are attributed OUTSIDE the symbol. Result: objdiff reports each such function as MATCH (body bytes identical) yet shows the function 2 bytes shorter in C, and a `.text` section delta of -2 per affected function (e.g. unk_02018000: 7 functions x -2 = -0xe). This is a layout-attribution artifact, NOT a real diff: the linker word-aligns each function so the final linked .text is byte-identical. ALWAYS confirm with `chiri pkg -- compare` (full ROM SHA1) — it passed for unk_02018000 despite the -14 objdiff section delta. Diagnose: arm-none-eabi-objdump -t both .o; the asm functions with -2 are exactly the ones whose asm source has a trailing `.balign 4, 0`. Distinct from [[objdiff-size-miscount-inline-jumptable]] (which is inline jump-table data miscounted as code).

### objdiff.py can falsely report a function SIZE mismatch when the function has an inline Thumb jump-table (data) region — verify byte-identity manually + via full compare  <!-- id: objdiff-jumptable-size-artifact -->

A Thumb switch emits an inline jump table (e.g. `.short case0..caseN` after `add pc, r1`) inside .text. objdiff delimits functions by symbol size; the asm .o marks the table with a $d data mapping symbol and may report a different symbol size than the C .o (e.g. sub_02096260 reported 176 vs 184), flagging a SIZE mismatch even though every instruction byte (and the table words 0008/0026/003c/0052/0090) is identical. The only real differences in the raw dump were the bl placeholders (fff7feff in the asm .o vs 00f000f8 in the C .o) which are unresolved relocations that link identically. Resolution: dump `arm-none-eabi-objdump -s -j .text` for both, compare non-bl bytes; then trust `chiri pkg -- compare` (full ROM SHA1) as authoritative. (unk_020961D8.s)

### A triage gated_by:[ipa-shared-headers] can be a FALSE POSITIVE when the shared symbols are common library IMPORTS, not exports of a mutable shared header  <!-- id: false-ipa-gate-shared-imports -->

triage flags a file as gated when it shares symbols with a blocked file. But check WHICH symbols: unk_020961D8.s was gated against unk_0200FA24.s, but the only shared .public symbols were Heap_Free and IsPaletteFadeFinished — ubiquitous imports, not a shared mutable header (the real ipa-shared-headers risk is the sound.h family). Confirm with: comm -12 of the two .inc .public lists; if the overlap is just common imports (Heap_*, memcpy, MI_*, palette/fade helpers), the gate is spurious and the file is safe to do alone. Bonus tell here: include/unk_020961D8.h already existed and a matched file (scrcmd_c.c) already called it, so the header was frozen — implement the .c only.

### If a frozen header uses fx32/VecFx32/MtxFx33 but #includes nothing for them, global.h may NOT provide them and clang-format pins the .c-matching header first — wrap `#include <nitro/fx.h>` before it in // clang-format off  <!-- id: frozen-header-fx32-include-order -->

global.h (force-included) does NOT reliably define fx32/VecFx32 — files that use them include <nitro/fx.h> explicitly (e.g. camera.c, and self-sufficient headers like camera.h include it themselves). unk_02020B8C.h is frozen and uses fx32 but includes nothing, so the includer must define fx32 BEFORE it. clang-format forces the header matching the .c filename to be the first include, so a plain `#include <nitro/fx.h>` gets reordered AFTER unk_02020B8C.h -> `undefined identifier fx32` (cascading parse errors into mi/memory.h, mi/dma.h). Fix: pin the order with `// clang-format off` / `// clang-format on` around `#include <nitro/fx.h>` then `#include "unk_02020B8C.h"`. (The fx/fx.h guard isnt pre-set, so the explicit include really does define the types.) Symptom signature: first error is fx32 undefined at the frozen header line, then a flood of undefined-identifier errors in unrelated nitro headers.

### objdiff 'SIZE mismatch' false positive: inline Thumb jump table + cross-section relocations  <!-- id: objdiff-false-positive-inline-jumptable-reloc -->

A function with an inline Thumb switch jump table (add pc,r0 then .short offset entries) can show as an objdiff SIZE/byte mismatch even when it is byte-identical after linking. Two causes: (1) the asm reference object has one merged .text so local `bl` targets are PC-encoded directly (f000 fXXX), while the MWCC -ipa file object emits per-function sections so every `bl` is a relocation placeholder (f000 f800) — these resolve to the same bytes at link; (2) objdump renders the jump-table bytes as a .word in the asm but as two .short/instructions in the C object, confusing objdiff's size measurement. Verify by normalizing reloc operands (sed 's/[0-9a-f]+ <[^>]+>/X/') before diffing, and ALWAYS trust `chiri pkg -- compare` (full ROM SHA1) over objdiff for these. Saw in ov01_021FB6C4 (overlay_01_021FB5D4.s): objdiff said 'SIZE 134 vs 138' but the full ROM matched.
